summary: Sonos has announced the new Beam Ultra mid-size soundbar, featuring a 7.1.2-channel configuration with two up-firing drivers for an upgraded Dolby Atmos experience. The device also includes a redesigned centre channel, AI Speech Enhancement, and music performance improvements, though it still lacks DTS:X support. Priced at £699, it sits between the Arc Ultra and the base Beam Gen 2, which will remain on sale.
key_points: The Sonos Beam Ultra features a 7.1.2-channel configuration with two up-firing drivers.
It includes a redesigned centre channel, four levels of AI Speech Enhancement, and a Night Sound setting.
The soundbar does not support DTS:X audio.
It will launch in the UK priced at £699 and is available in black and white finishes.
The base Sonos Beam Gen 2 will remain on sale below the new Ultra in Sonos' lineup.

title: Sony’s new party speakers have more bass, more LEDs, and more connectivity
author: Andrew Liszewski
content:
Sony announced three new tower-style party speakers that will now be the largest options in its ULT Power Sound lineup. The new ULT Tower Max, ULT Tower 7, and ULT Tower 5 all feature expanded connectivity including USB-C, RCA, and XLR ports for connecting to audio gear using physical cables. The new models also come with improved lighting using up to 100 LEDs to provide visual feedback for functions like battery life and Bluetooth syncing in addition to creating an animated light show synced to what you’re listening to.
Sony’s new party speakers have more bass, more LEDs, and more connectivity
The new Tower Max, Tower 7, and Tower 5 speakers have USB-C, XLR, and RCA ports to connect to gear that isn’t wireless.
![sonyspeaker1](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/sonyspeaker1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0.02498750624688%2C100%2C99.950024987506&w=2400)
![sonyspeaker1](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/sonyspeaker1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0.02498750624688%2C100%2C99.950024987506&w=2400)
![An access panel open on the back of the Sony ULT Tower 7 speaker showing various ports.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/sonyspeaker4.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
The largest of the new ULT Power Sound speakers is the $1,499.99, 121-pound Tower Max that looks big enough to double as a coffee table. Four tweeters, two midrange drivers, and three 280mm woofers work together to deliver what Sony describes as “the most powerful bass yet” in its ULT Power Sound collection.
![The Sony ULT Tower 7 party speaker sitting outside next to a table with DJ equipment surrounded by partyers.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/sonyspeaker3.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
All three of the new speakers feature four redesigned handles to improve portability while the Tower Max and Tower 7 also feature wider wheels for better maneuverability. For the first time users can also tweak the EQ settings for the speakers’ default sound profiles including ULT1 and ULT2 that maximize bass or the Flat mode that more accurately reproduces a song’s original mix with less of a chest-thumping experience.
![The Sony ULT Tower 5 party speaker on a rug next to a couch and DJ mixing pad.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/sonyspeaker2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
The 50-pound, $649.99 Tower 7 features a single 280mm woofer paired with two midrange drivers and four tweeters that can run for up to 30 hours on a built-in rechargeable battery with the LED lighting turned off. The smallest of the three new models is the 29-pound, $449.99 Tower 5 that offers up to 20 hours of battery-powered playback through a 230mm woofer, two midrange drivers, and a pair of tweeters. It also has the same IPX4 water-resistance as the Tower 7, but only when the speakers are used standing vertically. The Tower Max is only “splash proof” on its top panel so you’ll want to stick to using it indoors.
summary: Sony has announced three new tower-style party speakers joining its ULT Power Sound lineup: the ULT Tower Max, ULT Tower 7, and ULT Tower 5. These models feature expanded physical connectivity, up to 100 LEDs for lighting effects, redesigned handles, and customizable EQ settings. The speakers range in price and size, offering varying battery life, water-resistance levels, and acoustic driver configurations.
key_points: Sony announced three new tower speakers: ULT Tower Max ($1,499.99), Tower 7 ($649.99), and Tower 5 ($449.99).
The speakers include expanded physical connectivity options such as USB-C, RCA, and XLR ports.
Up to 100 LEDs provide animated light shows and visual feedback for functions like battery life and Bluetooth syncing.
Users can now tweak EQ settings for default sound profiles, including bass-heavy ULT modes and a Flat mode.
The Tower 7 offers up to 30 hours of battery life with lights off, while the Tower 5 offers up to 20 hours and features IPX4 water-resistance when vertical.

title: After two years of turmoil, Sonos attempts a triumphant return.
author: John Higgins
content:
At an event in New York City, Sonos announced two new audio products — the Sonos Beam Ultra soundbar and Sonos Ace Ultra headphones, details of which were found in an FCC filing in early August — and a major update to its audio operating system dubbed Sonos 27. It’s the biggest single Sonos announcement since 2024, when a new app rollout upset its customers and sent it into damage control mode.
Sonos introduces new headphones, soundbar, and software in its biggest announcement in years
After two years of turmoil, Sonos attempts a triumphant return.
![sonos-ace-ultra-lifestyle](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/sonos-ace-ultra-lifestyle.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0.041631973355535%2C100%2C99.916736053289&w=2400)
![sonos-ace-ultra-lifestyle](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/sonos-ace-ultra-lifestyle.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0.041631973355535%2C100%2C99.916736053289&w=2400)
Software changes are core to Sonos’ announcements, with the company leaning heavily into AI integration with Sonos 27. This includes the company’s own Sonos 27voice assistant that it built in-house for music and system control. It’s coming as an early access, opt-in feature this fall. There’s also Sonos 27mcp, which gives the ability to connect any existing AI models such as ChatGPT or Google Gemini — although for some reason Google Assistant is still not natively supported. Sonos 27mcp launches in early access on September 8th.
In addition, users will be able to create up to 10 of their own agents through Sonos 27 to run, with whichever model they choose. These custom agents can be given different voices and roles. Brandon Holley, senior director of product development, gave examples of having a moody detective give you the morning news or a motivational coach whisper motivational aspirations when you wake up. Custom agents won’t be available until sometime in 2027.
Both Sonos 27mcp and the custom agents seem to expand the customization and control of a Sonos system beyond what the app and Sonos 27voice is capable of.
![Hands holding a phone displaying the EQ setting on the Sonos app.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/sonos-app-eq.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
All products compatible with the current Sonos app can be controlled with Sonos 27mcp, and everything with a microphone works with Sonos 27voice. When the Sonos custom agents are available, they’ll work everywhere Sonos 27voice is enabled.
There are two new features being added to Sonos Fabric, which is the name given to its whole-home connected system. The wireless Play and Move 2 portable speakers can be used as surround sound speakers in a home theater system. Once in place, the speakers will automatically configure to their new positions and roles as surround speakers without needing to initiate setup in the Sonos app. It’s not possible to use this feature with a single Play or Move 2.
Compatible Sonos headphones will now be included in a Sonos home system and support moving sound between speakers and headphones — the system senses the closest speaker and will pass the audio from it to the headphones. Headphone linking, as Sonos calls it, will roll out as an early access feature on September 29th. Sonos hints that this is just the beginning of added features, but no further details about possible future options were given.
Improvements continue to come to the app, as well, again with feedback from the community, including the Sonos subreddit. Home, system, and search tabs will be added across the bottom of the screen, and a room sort option can be pinned to the top for easier access to a customizable list. There’s a cool feature that calls back to physical audio components: a virtual volume knob, you control with two fingers like you would in the real world. It’s not a major quality of life improvement, but it’s something that adds character and fun, and something I’ll probably use regularly. The new navigation, room sorts, and virtual volume knob starts rolling out on September 8 (although the volume knob will only launch on iOS at that time).
Lockscreen controls for volume and play/pause are also returning to the app, and started rolling out on August 17th. System health views to help troubleshoot issues and presets will roll out at some point later this fall.
It’s not just software announcements, though, as Sonos has two new products coming — the long-rumored Ace Ultra headphones and Beam Ultra soundbar.
![The Sonos Ace Ultra in white on a marble counter.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/sonos-ace-ultra-lifestyle-2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
The Sonos Ace Ultra are what the original Sonos Ace should have been from the beginning — an integrated part of the Sonos ecosystem. They are built upon Sonos’ Headphone Engine 2, which allows them to use the headphone linking feature rolling out at the same time as the headphones release on September 29th. A button on the headphones allows audio to be passed between a speaker and the headphones. No phone is necessary if it’s out of reach.
They look very similar to the Ace, with what appears to be slightly different button placement on the left ear cup. The Ace Ultra are also a little bigger, with a little more space in the ear cup, and 10 grams heavier. They have newly custom-designed 40mm drivers and 10 microphones for noise control (two more than the Ace) which Sonos claims makes their ANC twice as effective at noise cancellation than the Ace with “the frequencies that really matter,” as Brandon Holley told me. Those frequencies happen to be 65Hz (the general frequency of an HVAC) where the Sonos Ace Ultra are 2.2 times more effective, and 120Hz — the airplane drone range — where they’re 1.8 times better. No information is provided for performance with the chatter you might encounter at the coffee shop, for example.
An adaptive EQ adjusts the sound, compensating for any air leaks in the headphones’ fit due to glasses, jewelry, or hair. It includes both a 3-band and 8-band EQ to customize the sound for your taste. In addition to SBC and AAC codecs, the Ace Ultra supports aptX Adaptive Lossless over Bluetooth, and 16-bit/48kHz high resolution when connected with USB-C.
Battery life has improved by five hours, with the Sonos Ace Ultra offering up to 35 hours of listening with ANC on. A fast charge of three minutes gets an additional three hours of listening time.
Instead of just black and white, the Ace Ultra are also available in a muted blue agave and beige sand color. The headphones release on September 29th for $449.
![An angled shot of the Sonos Beam Ultra in black on a table under a TV.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/09/sonos-beam-ultra-lifestyle.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
The Beam Ultra is a completely redesigned 7.1.2 compact soundbar (as opposed to the 5.0 configuration of its predecessor), including two up-firing drivers to support Dolby Atmos spatial audio. The center channel mid-tweeter features a new waveguide, mechanic and acoustic design, and DSP, which includes four levels of AI speech enhancement for clarity.
While the Beam Ultra still has a compact design, to accommodate the additional speakers it is just under four inches longer than the Beam Gen 2. It comes in a black or white matte finish, and will be available for purchase on September 29th for $699.
With the headphones’ deeper integration into the Sonos ecosystem and the addition of up-firing drivers to the Beam Ultra, it looks like Sonos has made some great improvements to already solid products. But I won’t know for sure until I can dig into them for reviews. The app updates — particularly the AI integration — I’m a bit more cautious about. But Sonos is making the right move by rolling out the updates over time, allowing its users to opt in to early access instead of dumping it on everyone at once. This more measured approach could be what wins back the masses.
summary: At an event in New York City, Sonos announced a major return following two years of turmoil by introducing the Sonos Beam Ultra soundbar, Sonos Ace Ultra headphones, and the Sonos 27 operating system. The updates heavily feature AI integration, including an in-house voice assistant and support for external AI models like ChatGPT and Google Gemini. Additionally, Sonos is rolling out whole-home audio improvements, headphone linking, and app navigation updates with a measured, opt-in approach.
key_points: Sonos announced the Sonos Beam Ultra soundbar and Sonos Ace Ultra headphones, both launching on September 29th.
The new Sonos 27 operating system introduces an in-house voice assistant and Sonos 27mcp for connecting external AI models like ChatGPT and Google Gemini.
Wireless Play and Move 2 portable speakers can now automatically configure as surround sound speakers in a home theater setup.
The Sonos Ace Ultra headphones feature improved active noise cancellation, 35-hour battery life, and support for headphone linking with nearby speakers.
App navigation is being updated based on community feedback, introducing home, system, and search tabs, lockscreen controls, and a virtual volume knob.

title: What Dyson’s First Toothbrush Says About Oral Care’s Beauty Era
author: Karin Eldor
content:
Open wide: the luxury playbook that transformed skincare and haircare is coming for our mouths.
Dyson, the global brand known for its highly engineered everyday products, like blow dryers, fans and vacuums, is entering oral care with an electric toothbrush, called Dyson CameraJet. It’s the first toothbrush with a camera and a jet, combining brushing with technology designed to identify and clean the gaps between teeth, addressing a part of the routine consumers know matters, but often neglect. It’s the result of six years of research, development, and engineering, challenging every aspect of conventional oral care, says founder James Dyson. The Dyson CameraJet is also Wi-Fi connected at 2.4GHz, enabling users to watch as they brush through the MyDyson app.
For decades, oral care has only touched the surface of what’s possible, Dyson engineer Niamh Turney says. “On the whole, we’re seeing people cutting steps and trying to cut corners in their oral care routine. The cycle has been that way for decades. It’s a cycle of paste, brush, rinse, floss everyday, twice a day, and it’s just obvious it’s not working.” According to the World Health Organization’s 2025 Global Oral Health Status Report, nearly 3.7 billion people are estimated to be affected by oral diseases globally, while oral health is linked to overall health, as well as our microbiome.
By building interdental cleaning into brushing, the device makes that often-skipped step harder to avoid. “With this, you’re forced to be more methodical and it’s actually quite enjoyable,” Dyson says. “It’s probably the first product we’ve done where it actually takes longer than what it’s replacing.” The bet is that consumers will trade speed for a more thorough clean.
Oral care is already big business. The global market is valued at approximately $37.8 billion in 2024 and is expected to reach $54.1 billion by 2030. But beyond whitening, oral care has remained one of retail’s most clinical and commoditized categories, marketed through the unsexy language of cavities, plaque and gingivitis. A new generation of founders is borrowing from beauty and luxury to reposition toothpaste, mouthwash and breath care as aspirational products. Their language is sensorial, their packaging is designed to be displayed and their formulas emphasize hydration, ingredient literacy and the oral microbiome.
Dyson’s launch, meanwhile, points to a massive opportunity in premium oral care for brands: convincing consumers that one of their most regular, twice-daily habits deserves the same investment, discernment and pleasure as skincare.
Oral care’s glow up
New entries to the oral care category are taking a new approach, with an expanded focus on whole-mouth wellness, formulas and formats borrowed from beauty, and sensorial products designed to be displayed and enjoyed.
Köppen, the Ayurveda-inspired oral-care brand launched by siblings Parag and Priya Shah in spring 2026, reflects a broader shift beyond teeth with a whole-mouth system spanning everything from toothpaste and floss to oil pulling, mouth tape, lip balm and tongue scraping.
“The first thing we made was a copper tongue scraper because I couldn’t find one that felt like something I actually wanted to own,” says Parag Shah. “That product eventually reached tens of thousands of customers, but more importantly, it showed us that people were hungry for a different relationship with oral care. That became the larger idea behind Köppen: what would oral care look like if we completely reconsidered the category rather than simply making a better toothpaste?”
The category’s beauty repositioning extends to innovative hardware, echoing the rise of LED masks, microcurrent devices and facial-cleansing tools that have helped turn clinically inspired technology into coveted at-home beauty products. Oral-care brands are taking a similar approach to tools consumers use every day. Foreo already straddles both categories: its assortment includes the Luna 4 facial-cleansing and firming device and the Issa 4 Plus smart silicone sonic toothbrush. Flaus, meanwhile, has turned traditional floss into a rechargeable electric flosser.
Dyson is pushing the category further by combining a camera, precision water jets and Wi-Fi connectivity to integrate interdental cleaning into brushing.
“Flossing is an awkward and time-consuming chore. Few of us do it even though we know we should,” Dyson says. “Our research has shown that people consistently miss the areas where plaque forms: the gaps between teeth.”
With nine in 10 people not flossing as regularly as recommended and the average person brushing for just 45 seconds, according to a Dyson study — well below the two-minute guideline — the gap between recommendation and behavior creates an opportunity for products that make oral care more integrated and enjoyable.
That education is also driving interest in ingredients and the oral microbiome. Bastét’s French Mint Toothpaste contains 10% nano-hydroxyapatite, while its aluminium tube evokes the affordable luxury of “a Byredo candle, an Aesop soap, a luxury incense”, according to founder Alexandra Baker. “We’ve spent a decade learning about the gut microbiome and, more recently, the skin microbiome, but the oral microbiome is still treated like it only matters for cavities and bad breath,” she says.
Mouth Loob, a new take on mouthwash launching this fall, applies skincare language and formulation even more literally. Co-founders Ally Weiss and Ash Schroeder describe its hyaluronic acid-powered, pH-balanced and alcohol-free formula as “skincare for your mouth”. Its viscous, serum-like texture is designed to coat the tissues of the mouth, targeting dry mouth associated with factors including aging, hormonal changes, dehydration and medications such as GLP-1s.
Sensorial experience is becoming another point of differentiation. Orist is teasing its early 2027 launch under the tagline “It’s an oral fixation.” Its debut product, a toothpaste, was developed with both a flavourist and a chemist. “The mouth is the most sensorial part of the body,” says founder Jess Eggert.
Stockholm-based Selahatin has brought the language of fragrance — and the cachet of fashion — to oral care. Known for its sensual, design-led approach, the brand collaborated with Rick Owens on a four-piece collection last year. Its Eau d’Extrait Oral range includes portable breath sprays with names such as “Escapist” and “Of Course I Still Luv You”, packaged in the restrained, display-worthy style of brands such as Crown Affair and Salt & Stone.
Fraîche, meanwhile, is launching with a microbiome-friendly breath spray that founder Julie McDonnell positions as an immediate “confidence hit”. She wants to give breath spray the “Touchland treatment”: a portable beauty object designed to be used throughout the day.
Fraîche’s slim, flat packaging borrows from beauty codes, fitting as easily into a pocket as a Rhode lip tint. The wider category is adopting a similarly fashion-forward, sensual and sometimes provocative design language. Even names such as Bastét, Köppen, Orist and Fraîche sound more like fashion or fragrance houses than oral-care brands.
“Culture came first, science will make it stick, but aesthetics will drive the behavior change,” says McDonnell. These products are meant to be displayed, shared on social media and even flaunted — not relegated to the medicine cabinet. Their portability could also move oral care beyond the pharmacy aisle and into beauty and fashion retailers, checkout counters, gyms and coffee shops.
A new route into retail
For now, premium oral care remains on the fringes of dedicated beauty and wellness retail. Goop’s offering is limited to mouth tape, while Violet Grey and Ulta carry OLAS mouthwash. Credo has a broader assortment, mostly from oral brand Cocolab.
Instead, the category is finding a home at upmarket lifestyle grocers such as Erewhon and Happier Grocery.
Perhaps more tellingly, premium oral care is appearing at fashion and luxury retailers. Köppen is stocked at Revolve and FWRD (in addition to lifestyle grocer Laurel Supply), while Selahatin can be found at Holt Renfrew, Selfridges, Dover Street Market, Luisa Via Roma, Printemps New York and FWRD.
Trudy Arnold, head of beauty and home at Revolve and FWRD, says the retailers began noticing the shift in 2024, as interest expanded beyond toothpaste and whitening into tongue scraping, mouth rinses, oil pulling, electric toothbrushes and ingredient-conscious formulas.
“For Revolve, oral care must offer performance and cultural relevance; for FWRD, the lens is discovery, craftsmanship and an elevated experience,” Arnold says. “Ultimately, across both brands, we’re looking for products that work, have a clear reason to exist and make an everyday routine feel more considered.”
The Dyson CameraJet will be available through Dyson direct channels (Dyson.com and Dyson Demo Stores), as well as Amazon, Costco, Best Buy, and Sephora — marking the beauty retailer’s official entry into the category. For Dyson, the launch extends beyond the toothbrush itself: the company has developed proprietary non-foaming toothpaste and mouth rinse to optimize visibility for the toothbrush’s one-millimeter-square camera.
The launch may be just the beginning. “We see that there are more things we can do in this space,” Dyson says.
summary: Dyson is entering the oral care market with the Dyson CameraJet, an electric toothbrush featuring a built-in camera and water jet designed to improve interdental cleaning. This launch coincides with a broader industry trend where brands are borrowing luxury and beauty playbooks to transform traditional oral hygiene into an aspirational, sensorial experience. Emerging startups and hardware makers are introducing whole-mouth wellness products, design-forward packaging, and ingredient-focused formulas that are finding retail spaces in fashion boutiques and lifestyle stores.
key_points: Dyson developed the CameraJet electric toothbrush over six years, combining a camera, precision water jets, and Wi-Fi connectivity to make interdental cleaning part of the brushing routine.
The global oral care market was valued at approximately $37.8 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach $54.1 billion by 2030.
New oral care brands are adopting aesthetics, formulas, and terminology from the beauty and fragrance sectors, emphasizing the oral microbiome, sensorial experiences, and display-worthy packaging.
Premium oral care products are expanding beyond traditional pharmacies and into fashion retailers, luxury stores, and upscale lifestyle grocers like Revolve, Selfridges, and Erewhon.

title: "No such thing as a luxury track car..." - I've driven the Bentley Supersports, and I disagree | Autocar
author: Matt Saunders
content:
It’s unlikely that the latest addition to the Bentley Continental model range was born out of wondering how, exactly, to top the power-to-weight ratio of a Continental GT Speed. But if it had been, and you the bold/foolhardy young buck in the ideas meeting who’d suggested beginning by taking away a-hundred-and-something horsepower, you wouldn’t have expected to be listened to – or, even, gainfully employed – for very long.
But that, in one very simple sense, is what’s happened to the Continental GT in order to turn it into the new Bentley Supersports (note the dropping of the ‘Continental GT’ part of the model name here; perhaps simply because Bentley wanted the new one – in the spirit of the car – to be quicker to say).
That’s an awfully long way from all that has happened to this car, mind you. Bentley has never before demonstrated anything like the commitment to serve the interests of keen drivers that it has just shown by bringing to the brink of sale this very special, at-least-relatively-lightweight, two-seat Continental.
The new Supersports – only 500 examples of which will be made, with deliveries beginning just before the end of 2026 – has been championed by former Porsche executive turned Bentley CEO Frank Walliser as something of a catalyst. A means of demonstrating the untapped capabilities of his company; the latent potential of its cars; and the readiness of its customer base to embrace special derivatives of first-order performance flavouring. It handles the first two feats pretty well, in this tester’s estimation. The hot-ticket sales reception with which it has been met suggests the third is something of a formality.
summary: Bentley has introduced the new Supersports, a special two-seat version of its Continental model range that departs from tradition by prioritizing driver engagement and a relatively lightweight build. Championed by CEO Frank Walliser, the vehicle showcases the brand's latent performance capabilities to a receptive customer base. Production is limited to 500 units, with deliveries scheduled to begin before the end of 2026.
key_points: The new Bentley Supersports drops 'Continental GT' from its name for brevity.
Only 500 examples of the car will be produced.
Deliveries for the Supersports are set to begin just before the end of 2026.
The car was championed by Bentley CEO Frank Walliser to demonstrate the brand's performance potential.

title: Roundup: The First Reviews Have Dropped For Onimusha: Way Of The Sword, And They're Very Good
author: Pure Xbox; Craig Reid
content:
![Roundup: The First Reviews Have Dropped For Onimusha: Way Of The Sword, And They're Very Good 1](https://images.purexbox.com/85ac3f5dbe4ac/roundup-the-first-reviews-have-dropped-for-onimusha-way-of-the-sword-and-theyre-very-good-1.900x.jpg)
Well, well, well, reviews are in for Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and they're looking pretty darned good!
Capcom's latest title revives the dark samurai series for a modern audience, and it's currently holding a stellar Metacritic rating of 88 on Nintendo Switch 2, 86 on PS5, 82 on PC. It's yet to be rated for Xbox, with only two reviews available right now, bring the overall score to a whopping 86!
So, how about we get stuck into what the critics are saying about Onimusha: Way of the Sword:
Hey Poor Player (10/10)
"Onimusha: Way of the Sword is a visually stunning revival that successfully brings Capcom’s classic franchise into the modern era using the RE Engine. Musashi injects a refreshing sense of personality into dark fantasy Kyoto, especially during the game’s intense and cinematic boss fights. This is definitely an action adventure game of the year contender."
MonsterVine (10/10)
"Onimusha: Way of the Sword is easily a contender for game of the year, as it blends merciless action with skill-based combat in a near-seamless way. The story and visuals complement the ridiculously sharp gameplay extremely well, and though the camera can be a little problematic on rare occasions, that shouldn’t stop you from experiencing Capcom’s latest banger."
Nintendo Life (9/10)
"Onimusha: Way of the Sword is a successful revival of Capcom's samurai franchise that pushes its gameplay in an exciting new direction while still retaining its core identity. The slower, more deliberate combat feels great, especially when you manage several deflections in quick succession before slicing your foe in half. Glorious. Not everything works. The English voiceover doesn't quite fit with the overall presentation, while occasional jaunts to and from multiple NPCs threaten to derail the otherwise excellent pacing. These are minor gripes though; Onimusha is back baby, and it's better than ever."
summary: The first reviews have been released for Capcom's Onimusha: Way of the Sword, with critics praising the dark samurai series revival. The game has achieved strong Metacritic scores across platforms, including 88 on Nintendo Switch 2, 86 on PS5, and 82 on PC. Reviewers highlighted its stunning visuals, skill-based combat, and cinematic boss fights, despite minor issues with the camera and English voiceover.
key_points: Onimusha: Way of the Sword successfully revives Capcom's classic franchise for a modern audience.
The game holds strong Metacritic ratings, including 88 on Nintendo Switch 2, 86 on PS5, and 82 on PC.
Critics praised the title's visuals, RE Engine utilization, and skill-based combat.
Minor criticisms included occasional camera issues, mismatched English voiceovers, and pacing dips involving NPCs.

title: Castle launches four new speakers that offer "a new level of performance"
author: Ioan Hazell
content:
![Castle Walmer Series speakers on grey background featuring pairs of Castle Walmer 1 and 2](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/P4yi5L7v7RYixaDci8SBY9.jpg) 
British loudspeaker manufacturer, Castle, has announced two new series of speakers, Tintagel and Walmer, each featuring one standmounter and one floorstanding model.
According to Castle, the Tintagel Series is “the accessible bedrock of Castle’s new line-up”, while the Walmer Series is positioned further upmarket, “utilising sophisticated material and technologies” for “a new level of performance”.
The four new models are the first loudspeakers from Castle since the Windsor Series released in 2023. Like the Windsor Series, all of the new speakers will be designed and manufactured in the UK.
The new Tintagel series aims to bring Castle's "typical warmth, craft and musicality" in hand-crafted cabinets that use real-wood veneers.
 ![Castle Tintagel 1](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/KnLkNodEfXQpFWuHYARtyU.jpg) 
The Tintagel 1 is a two-way standmounter, with 13cm mid/bass advanced fibre driver and a 28mm silk dome tweeter. The speaker uses a large, rear-firing bass port for low frequency extension.
The Tintagel 2 floorstanders use a twin 15cm advanced fibre drivers alongside the same 28mm silk dome tweeter as the Tintagel 1. A downward-firing port runs through the speaker’s plinth, which Castle says makes the Tintagel 2 “easier to position” in your listening room.
The speakers’ 'advanced fibre' cones are made from a fibre blend designed to provide light weight and diaphragm damping. Castle says that the cones’ material qualities “avoid the hard, exposed character that can come from less controlled diaphragm materials”.
The latest hi-fi, home cinema and tech news, reviews, buying advice and deals, direct to your inbox.
The silk dome tweeters use a large dome and shallow waveguide to control high-frequency dispersion for “a stable tonal balance, both on and off axis”.
 ![Castle Walmer 1 on grey background](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/qb3HVoWqCtaB96tbxByhe.jpg) 
The more expensive Walmer Series features two speakers, the Walmer 1 and Walmer 2, which are designed for listeners who want more "technical refinement" and greater speed, openness and scale above the Tintagel models.
The Walmer 1 is a two-way standmount speaker, featuring a 13cm woven carbon fibre mid/bass driver and a 12x45mm ribbon tweeter. The three-way Walmer 2 floorstanders, on the other hand, use the same ribbon tweeter and twin 15cm bass drivers and a 11.5cm midrange unit, both made from woven carbon fibre.
Ribbon tweeters were chosen for the Walmer Series speakers due to their lightweight diaphragms, which can “respond quickly to resolve fine detail with delicacy and natural extension", while it also offers a wider horizontal dispersion of sound.
The drivers' carbon fibre material has a high stiffness-to-weight ratio, which Castle says delivers “bass notes [with] cleaner leading edges, reduces low-level colouration and allows the midrange to retain fine detail without becoming brittle”.
The Walmer 2’s midrange unit is also housed in its own enclosure, which isolates the driver from low frequency pressure changes inside the cabinet, “elevating clarity through the most critical part of the audio band”.
Additionally, the Walmer 2 featues a mass loaded transmission line system for controlled bass extension. Castle says the objective was to retain the brand's "natural warmth and musical ease" while also adding precision and transparency without sounding overly analytical.
The Castle Tintagel and Walmer Series are available from September, in finishes of Walnut and Black Oak. Prices are as follows:
Tintagel 1: £1999 / $2749 / AU$3749 per pair
Tintagel 2: £2999 / $3999 / AU$5499 per pair
Walmer 1: £2499 / $3499 / AU$4748 per pair
Walmer 2: £4999 / $7499 / AU$10,499 per pair

Ioan Hazell is a staff writer at What Hi-Fi?. He has previously written for The Sunday Times Culture Magazine, Museum's Journal, and a number of arts and culture publications. Outside of work, he is generally found cycling, writing, or gigging.

summary: British loudspeaker manufacturer Castle has announced four new models across two series, Tintagel and Walmer, marking its first speaker releases since 2023. Both series feature one standmounting and one floorstanding model, and all are designed and manufactured in the UK. The Tintagel series offers an accessible option with hand-crafted real-wood veneer cabinets, while the upmarket Walmer series utilizes advanced materials like woven carbon fibre and ribbon tweeters for higher performance.
key_points: Castle introduced four new loudspeakers divided into the Tintagel and Walmer series.
All new models are designed and manufactured in the UK and will be available starting in September.
The Tintagel series features advanced fibre drivers and silk dome tweeters, housed in hand-crafted real-wood veneer cabinets.
The upmarket Walmer series utilizes woven carbon fibre drivers, ribbon tweeters, and specialized internal enclosures for enhanced precision and clarity.

title: Just get a Pixel 11? Here are the first 10 settings you need to change
author: Sanuj Bhatia
content:
Just get a Pixel 11? Here are the first 10 settings you need to change
Aug 30, 2026 — 7:00 AM ET
![google pixel 11 pro canyon 6 Someone holding the Canyon Pixel 11 Pro.](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/google-pixel-11-pro-canyon-6-scaled.jpg)
The Google Pixel 11 series is officially out in the wild. As with pretty much every Pixel Google has released before, the new phones aren’t necessarily set up to give you the best experience out of the box.
There are plenty of useful features and settings that are either disabled by default or require manual configuration. And with the Pixel 11 series bringing a heap of new software features, there are even more things worth tweaking this year.
So, if you’ve just picked up a new Pixel 11, here are 10 settings and features I’d recommend changing right away.
Which new Pixel 11 feature are you most excited to try?
Customize your photos with Camera Looks
![google pixel 11 pro camera looks hands on 4 Using Camera Looks on the Google Pixel 11 Pro.](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/google-pixel-11-pro-camera-looks-hands-on-4-scaled.jpg)
Pixel phones have long been known for their cameras, and with the Pixel 11 series, Google is giving you more control over how those photos actually look with a new feature called Camera Looks.
Instead of applying a filter after taking the photo, Camera Looks lets you choose the overall color and tone before you shoot. For the “Default Look,” you can choose between four different levels of HDR processing. Additionally, you can swipe through more stylized Looks that have a much bigger impact on colors, contrast, etc.
The feature defaults to the “standard” style we’ve always had, though, so you’ll need to change it yourself:
- Open the Camera app.
- Tap the Settings icon in the bottom-right corner.
- Tap Looks.
- Swipe through the available styles and choose whichever one you want to use as your default.
Turn on the new Creator Suite tools
![pixel 11 creator suite 1 Pixel 11 camera app open on the Creator video settings tab](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/pixel-11-creator-suite-1.jpg)
Google has also focused heavily on social media creators with the Pixel 11 camera. There’s now a built-in teleprompter that lets you read a script directly from the screen while recording, along with social media grid lines that show where things like usernames, captions, Like buttons, and other UI elements will appear once you upload the video. It’s something you don’t even get natively on the iPhone right now.
These tools aren’t enabled by default, though. To enable these features:
- Open the Camera app.
- Switch to Video.
- Tap Settings.
- Head into the Creator tab.
- From there, you can enable whichever creator features you want to use.
Set up Extreme Charging
![pixel 11 extreme charging setup Pixel 11 displaying the Extreme Charging Mode setup screen](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/pixel-11-extreme-charging-setup.jpg)
While Google hasn’t dramatically increased battery capacities this year, it has quietly added a useful charging feature called Extreme Charging. Similar to features we’ve seen from OnePlus, Oppo, and Vivo, Extreme Charging lets the Pixel temporarily prioritize faster charging when you’re in a hurry. There are a couple of catches, though.
Extreme Charging only works when your battery is below 50%, and unfortunately, you’ll need to manually enable it every time you want the faster charging speed.
To enable it, plug in your Pixel when the battery is below 50%, then head to Settings > Battery & charging > Extreme Charging and tap Turn on now.
Show the exact battery percentage
![pixel 11 battery percentage toggle Hand holding Pixel 11 with battery percentage toggle enabled in settings](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/pixel-11-battery-percentage-toggle.jpg)
While you’re already inside the Battery settings, I’d also recommend enabling the battery percentage.
For some reason, Pixel phones still don’t show the exact battery percentage in the status bar by default. Personally, I’d much rather know exactly how much battery I have left than try to judge it from a tiny icon.
To do this, head to Settings > Battery & charging and enable the Battery Percentage toggle.
Customize HiLight for your favorite contacts
![google pixel 11 pro hilight color picker edited Color picker for HiLight on the Pixel 11 Pro.](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/google-pixel-11-pro-hilight-color-picker-edited-scaled.jpg)
One of the more interesting additions to the Pixel 11 Pro models is HiLight, Google’s new multicolor LED on the back. The light can activate when you’re using Gemini with the phone face down, but it can also display different colors depending on who’s calling. The catch is that you’ll need to assign those colors yourself.
- Open the Phone app.
- Select the contact you want to customize.
- Find HiLight Color inside the Contact settings.
- Choose a color and tap Done.
It’s also worth noting that you can only use HiLight for contacts you have favorited. To do this, select a contact and tap the star icon at the top of the page. Once you do this, the HiLight option will appear.
Let your Pixel escape bad Wi-Fi automatically
![pixel 11 adaptive connectivity Pixel 11 adaptive connectivity settings screen showing network toggles](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/pixel-11-adaptive-connectivity.jpg)
Google has finally switched to a MediaTek modem with the Pixel 11 series, but there’s another setting worth enabling if you want the most reliable internet connection possible: Adaptive Connectivity.
When you’re connected to a weak Wi-Fi network, your Pixel can automatically switch over to cellular data to give you a faster connection rather than keeping you stuck on painfully slow Wi-Fi. It’s particularly useful when you’re moving around your house or somewhere with patchy Wi-Fi coverage.
Head to Settings > Network & internet > Adaptive Connectivity, then enable Auto switch to mobile network.
Never lose a notification again
![pixel 11 notification history 1 Pixel 11 notification history screen listing recently dismissed alerts](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/pixel-11-notification-history-1.jpg)
If you get bombarded with notifications throughout the day, chances are you’ve swiped all of them away at some point, only to realize that one of them was actually important.
Thankfully, Android has a feature called Notification History that keeps a record of the notifications you’ve recently received, including the ones you’ve dismissed. Unfortunately, it’s disabled by default. To enable the feature:
- Open Settings.
- Tap Notifications.
- Tap Notification History.
- Tap the toggle next to Use notification history.
Like other Pixel phones, the Pixel 11 supports AI-powered notification summaries. These use the on-device Gemini model to condense longer notifications into something easier to read quickly, and you can enable them in the Notifications settings as well.
Make your lock screen useful with widgets
![pixel 11 lock screen widgets Pixel 11 lock screen showing weather, stock, and task widgets](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/pixel-11-lock-screen-widgets.jpg)
With Android 16 last year, Google finally brought lock screen widgets back to Pixel phones. The problem is that lock screen widgets are still disabled by default, even on the Pixel 11, so you’ll need to enable them manually.
To set up lock screen widgets:
- Open Settings.
- Tap Wallpaper & style.
- Scroll down and select More lock screen settings.
- Tap Widgets on lock screen.
Once enabled, whenever your phone is on the lock screen, you can swipe right to access your favorite widgets without unlocking the device. For example, I’ve added widgets for stocks, weather, and Google Tasks so I can quickly access all of them directly from my lock screen.
While you’re already inside the lock screen settings, I’d also recommend setting up the lock screen shortcuts. Head into Shortcuts, and from there you can customize what appears on both the left and right sides of your lock screen.
Don’t forget about Now Playing
![google pixel now playing app hero 1 The new Now Playing UI on a Pixel phone's lock screen.](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/google-pixel-now-playing-app-hero-1-scaled.jpg)
It’s 2026, and Now Playing remains one of my favorite underrated Pixel features.
The feature automatically identifies songs playing around you and displays the title directly on your lock screen. It also keeps a history of songs you’ve heard, which is incredibly useful when you hear something you like at a cafe or restaurant and forget to look it up immediately.
On the Pixel 11, Now Playing is easier to find than before, thanks to its dedicated app. To ensure the feature is set up:
- Open your app drawer and tap the Now Playing app.
- Tap the settings icon in the top-right corner.
- Tap Use Now Playing if it’s not currently enabled.
Set up Emergency features
![pixel 11 car crash detection Pixel 11 showing the Car Crash Detection feature setup screen](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/pixel-11-car-crash-detection.jpg)
Finally, there’s one setting I hope you’ll never need to use, but everyone should still configure: the built-in emergency features on your Pixel 11, such as Car Crash Detection.
If your Pixel detects that you’ve been involved in a serious car crash, it can vibrate, sound an alarm, and ask whether you need help. If you confirm that you do or don’t respond, the phone can contact emergency services and share your location with your emergency contacts.
To enable this, head over to Settings > Safety & emergency > Car Crash Detection and enable the toggle. Optionally, you can enable the Emergency Sharing toggle, which automatically shares your location with your emergency contacts.
It’s one of those features you could enable today and completely forget about afterward. Hopefully, you’ll never need it, but if you ever do, having it already configured could make a huge difference.
These are some of the settings I’d recommend changing as soon as you set up your new Pixel 11. Of course, there are plenty of other Pixel settings worth tweaking, but these should get you started.
Which one are you changing first? Let us know in the comments below.
summary: The Google Pixel 11 series offers many new and existing features that require manual configuration because they are disabled out of the box. Users can enhance their experience by adjusting camera tools, charging preferences, display settings, and safety features. Properly configuring these options helps unlock the full potential of the new hardware and software.
key_points: New Camera Looks and Creator Suite tools let users customize photo tones and utilize built-in teleprompter and grid features.
Extreme Charging and battery percentage toggles give users better control over battery monitoring and fast charging when the battery is below 50%.
Adaptive Connectivity allows the Pixel 11 to automatically switch from weak Wi-Fi to cellular data for a reliable internet connection.
Notification history and lock screen widgets must be manually enabled to prevent lost alerts and provide quick access to apps.
Emergency options like Car Crash Detection and Emergency Sharing should be configured under safety settings for critical situations.

title: Gems, ghosts and GTA VI: the biggest video games for autumn 2026
author: Jordan Erica Webber; Keith Stuart
content:
Onimusha: Way of the Sword
After 20 years away, Capcom’s hyper kinetic action adventure returns, pitting skilled samurai Miyamoto Musashi against hordes of warriors and demons in Edo-period Kyoto. Master the complex combat then prepare for flashing blades, disembodied limbs and geysers of spraying blood.
 
Screenbound
Billed as the first ever 5D platformer, Screenbound has you navigating a 3D landscape while simultaneously playing an on-screen handheld console, which contains a 2D mirror world. Everything you do in one affects the other in mind-bending ways. The most ingenious puzzle game we’ve seen in a long time.
 
![Screenbound](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/b4ade6c806404f9fcd992be23477db22b5b369a2/741_0_3598_2880/master/3598.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Marvel’s Wolverine
The team behind the brilliant Marvel’s Spider-Man titles is back with a very different kind of hero. The open-world New York setting is gone in favour of a globe-trotting narrative following Logan on his quest to protect vulnerable mutants. The visuals are gorgeous, while the slick combat brings literal meaning to the term bleeding edge.
 
Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave
The tactical role-playing adventure series returns to the realm explored in the acclaimed Fire Emblem: Three Houses. This time, hopeful contestants arrive at the glorious city of Dagsion to compete in a contest where the winner is granted a single wish. Deep combat, lush settings and fraught relationships are guaranteed.
  
Silent Hill comes to the east coast of Scotland in a beautifully gloomy new horror adventure. You play as Simon Ordell, returning to a quiet harbour town with no memory of whatever catastrophe has taken place there. The place seems abandoned, but you are not alone for long …
 
![Silent Hill: Townfall.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/e36ec9fb9a28aad9d646f6ec14874cc82f8331cc/297_0_1406_1125/master/1406.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Control Resonant
Remedy Entertainment sets out to disprove the notion that all video game sequels are more of the same. This follow-up to the successful 2019 sci-fi shooter has a new lead character with supernatural powers, a whole new role-playing adventure feel, and a fresh take on Manhattan, where a reality-bending monster awaits …
  
Ratatan
The latest gorgeously strange game from Patapon creator Hiroyuki Kotani is a rhythm action platformer set in a colourful world where enemies are defeated with songs and players can work together to produce devastating melodies. Imagine Dead Cells merged with PaRappa the Rapper and you’re getting close.
 
The world-beating mega shooter packs its bags full of guns, grenades and macho dialogue and heads for Korea, in another Modern Warfare instalment. There will be epic battles, sanitised politically adjacent themes and rip-roaring online multiplayer – plus, moustached SAS figurehead Captain Price will be tagging along for the ride. Resistance is futile.
 
Grand Theft Auto VI
After a decade in development and several delays, Rockstar’s entertainment behemoth returns, following loved-up criminals Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos as they take on every scumbag Vice City has to offer. Already looking vibrant, expansive and lascivious, this is Bonnie and Clyde for the digital generation.
summary: The article previews several major video games slated for release, highlighting diverse titles across various genres. Notable mentions include the return of Capcom's Onimusha series, a globe-trotting Marvel's Wolverine adventure, and Rockstar's long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI. Other highlighted games feature innovative mechanics, such as the 5D platformer Screenbound and the rhythm action game Ratatan.
key_points: Capcom is reviving the Onimusha action adventure series after a 20-year hiatus.
Marvel's Wolverine shifts from an open-world setting to a globe-trotting narrative.
Screenbound introduces a unique 5D puzzle platforming mechanic linking 3D and 2D worlds.
Grand Theft Auto VI follows criminals Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos in Vice City.
Ratatan combines rhythm action and platforming inspired by Patapon and other titles.

title: GTA VI Extended Gameplay Preview Attracted Over 4 Million Live Viewers
author: Cpt Jank Discuss
content:
Sunday, August 30th 2026
	
		
![Rockstar Games](https://tpucdn.com/images/news/rockstargames-v1788110601.png) 
It's been known since Rockstar released the first trailer for GTA VI that the upcoming action game would have a massive impact on the gaming industry, and analysts have predicted week-one sales of $4.5 billion when the game launches in November. Following Rockstar's GTA VI showcase at Gamescom, reports have emerged that, between Netflix, YouTube, and Twitch, nearly 4 million users tuned into the live show—a number that had ripple effects across the internet. 
For starters, in the two days since the GTA VI Extended Look video launched on YouTube, it has racked up over 14 million views, while Streams Charts, a tracker for Twitch stream data, reported 3,970,738 peak stream viewers of the Extended Gameplay stream across both the official and unofficial commentary live streams and watch parties for the three hours it tracked viewership.

summary: Rockstar Games' recent GTA VI extended gameplay showcase at Gamescom attracted nearly 4 million peak live viewers across platforms like Netflix, YouTube, and Twitch. The massive interest generated widespread internet traffic surges, including over 14 million views on YouTube within two days and login issues for some users. Analysts have previously predicted that the upcoming November game launch will achieve week-one sales of $4.5 billion.
key_points: Streams Charts reported a peak of 3,970,738 live viewers during the three-hour GTA VI Extended Gameplay stream.
The GTA VI Extended Look video accumulated over 14 million views on YouTube in its first two days.
Cloudflare reported traffic increases of 16% for Netflix, 12% for Twitch, and 39% for YouTube during the event.
Rockstar's official website experienced a 172% global traffic increase following the trailer's launch.
Analysts predict week-one sales of $4.5 billion when GTA VI launches in November.

title: Report: Apple Watch Series 12 may feature always-on heart-rate tracking, new Fitness app - 9to5Mac
author: Michael Burkhardt
content:
![Apple Watch Heart Rate app watchOS 10](https://9to5mac.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2023/07/apple-watch-heart-rate-app-watchos-10.jpeg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600) 
According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has a couple new features in the pipeline for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 that’ll make it much more appealing for health-conscious users. The company is also testing two finishes for the rumored ceramic version.
New health upgrades
These two key health upgrades will likely sound appealing if you’re someone who’s dissatisfied with the state of Apple Watch as a fitness tracker. The two features are always-on heart-rate tracking, and an all new app design. that’ll make it much easier to learn from your health data. Here’s how Gurman describes the new app:
Apple is also working on revamping its fitness and health app software to show more wellness-related metrics in a similar fashion to increasingly popular app offerings from Whoop and Oura.
As someone who currently owns a WHOOP, I will say my primary draw to it has always been the fact that I find it much easier to learn from my health data in the WHOOP app. It’ll show me all of the factors that make my sleep or recovery poor, whereas with Apple Watch it feels the only important thing is your activity rings. If Apple makes meaningful progress in this regard, I’ll be quite happy.
A key part of making the Apple Watch a more data-rich experience is well, having more data. Apple is reportedly testing the ability for the heart-rate sensor to record all day, rather than only during workouts and at random.
Two new finishes
We’ve already heard that Apple is weighing ceramic for the Apple Watch Series 12, though Gurman is now reporting that there’ll be two color options: the traditional white, as well as a dark gray color. There’ll also be “many new band colors and configurations.”
![](https://9to5mac.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2026/08/apple-watch-ceramic-s5.jpg?quality=82&strip=all)
Redesign in the future
The current Apple Watch design language was introduced in 2024, with the Apple Watch Series 12. It was a relatively modest shift, with the company making the watch much thinner at the compromise of bezels. According to Bloomberg, we may see a new Apple Watch redesign next year with the Series 13, though it could shift to the Series 14:
Apple is pushing to have a big redesign for its watch ready by next year, but things could still slip to the year after.
I am quite excited to see what Apple cooks up here. It does feel like they’ve about peaked at what they can do with the rounded off design language, so maybe we’ll see a new shape entirely. Hopefully it doesn’t break backwards compatibility with older watch bands.

title: 12 TB Valve Archive Leaks Online, Fans Dig Through Early Portal 2 and Half-Life Clues
author: DrUsmanSaleem Discuss
content:
Sunday, August 30th 2026
	
		
![Steam](https://tpucdn.com/images/news/steam-v1788110601.png) 
A gigantic 12-terabyte archive from Valve's old Steam2 content servers has leaked online, containing internal development builds spanning from 2003 to 2013. The trove includes a July 2009 build of Portal 2 with unused sequences and beta menus, along with assets from F-Stop, the canceled Portal prequel. There's also a playable 2008 build of Left 4 Dead and early Counter-Strike: Global Offensive content. 
The most talked-about find is a "Weaponizer" model appearing in the Portal 2 files, long rumored to be a concept weapon from the canceled Half-Life 2: Episode Three. The model has surfaced before, but never inside an actual game build, so its presence here is of some significance. However, it may simply have been repurposed as an unrelated placeholder asset.
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/k11Sz7a16mD4EZB8_thm.jpg) 
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/2fAWE66pIlAf7fR1_thm.jpg) 
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/4Lv146iCgiGXZxft_thm.jpg) Contrary to how it may appear at first, the leak wasn't the result of a hack. It comes from an old, publicly accessible Steam2 endpoint that Valve apparently never took offline after migrating to SteamPipe in 2013. Valve hasn't commented on this leak, and given the size of the archive, it will likely take the community days or weeks to fully sort through everything inside it.

				Gabe Follower on X

summary: A 12-terabyte archive of Valve's internal development builds from 2003 to 2013 leaked online from an unclosed Steam2 endpoint. Fans are currently combing through the massive trove, which features early builds and assets for games like Portal 2, Left 4 Dead, and Counter-Strike: Global Offensive. Valve has not yet commented on the incident.
key_points: A 12-terabyte archive from Valve's old Steam2 content servers leaked online.
The leak stems from an old, publicly accessible endpoint left active after migrating to SteamPipe in 2013.
The archive includes a 2009 Portal 2 build, assets from the canceled prequel F-Stop, a 2008 Left 4 Dead build, and CS:GO content.
Fans discovered a "Weaponizer" model in the Portal 2 files linked to the canceled Half-Life 2: Episode Three.
Valve has not issued any comments regarding the leak.

title: A massive Valve leak has surfaced online, and fans are already hunting for Half-Life 2: Episode Three clues
author: Vikki Blake
content:
A leaked archive said to contain around 12TB of old Valve development files, dated between 2003 and 2013, has surfaced online, and fans are already combing through it for any trace of the long-cancelled Half-Life 2: Episode Three.
The leak was first flagged on Friday by Twitter/X user Gabe Follower, who said the archive included early versions of Portal 2, Left 4 Dead, and CS:GO, along with assets from the cancelled Portal prequel F-Stop, and "potentially" material tied to Episode Three.
Someone leaked 12 TB of Valve's internal builds and game assets from 2003 to 2013. This includes early versions of Portal 2, Left 4 Dead, CS:GO, F-Stop and potentially EP3. The community is still researching everything, so the next few days might be insane... There's a Weaponizer… pic.twitter.com/Sg7OqJjL2X
— Gabe Follower (@gabefollower) August 29, 2026
So far, the leak is thought to contain a 2009-era Portal 2 beta build alongside a model for the "Weaponizer", a weapon previously associated (if never confirmed) with Episode Three, though here apparently repurposed as a placeholder asset within Portal 2 itself.
Elsewhere in the archive, people have identified a fully playable Left 4 Dead beta build dated June 2008, complete with an early HUD, a work-in-progress lobby screen, and cut audio, including lines originally recorded for Zoey by Alésia Glidewell before Jen Taylor replaced her in the final game.
The material reportedly comes from Valve's old Steam2 content-delivery infrastructure, which the studio phased out in favour of SteamPipe in the early 2010s.
This differs from the cyber attack Valve disclosed earlier this month, when its European shipping partner, CEVA Logistics, was breached and hardware customers' personal details were exposed, rather than any of Valve's own game data. Valve hasn't commented on this latest leak.
With 12TB to work through, it'll likely be days before the community has any clearer picture of exactly what's in there, Episode Three included.
We already had an inkling – if, admittedly, no specific confirmation – that Valve is working on a major new Half-Life project of some kind. After a trustworthy report in 2024 detailed datamined assets, backing up a leak from an actor likely involved, we were told the new Half-Life project, codenamed HLX, was not just in development but now "playable, end-to-end".
What we do know for sure is Half-Life 3 was in development 2013/2014, and was set to be a procedurally-generated, replayable game that fused Left 4 Dead-inspired gameplay with scripted story moments. It was cancelled because it was built on the unfinished Source 2 engine.
summary: A massive 12TB archive of Valve development files spanning from 2003 to 2013 has leaked online, prompting fans to search for clues regarding the cancelled Half-Life 2: Episode Three. The leaked material includes early versions of Portal 2, Left 4 Dead, and CS:GO, alongside a 2009 Portal 2 beta build featuring a placeholder 'Weaponizer' model. The files reportedly originate from Valve's retired Steam2 content-delivery infrastructure, distinct from a recent breach at a European shipping partner. Valve has not yet commented on the leak.
key_points: A leaked archive containing roughly 12TB of Valve development files from 2003 to 2013 surfaced online.
Fans are currently searching the files for any references to the cancelled Half-Life 2: Episode Three.
The leak includes early builds of games like Portal 2, Left 4 Dead, and CS:GO.
The material is believed to come from Valve's old Steam2 content-delivery infrastructure.
Valve has not issued a comment regarding the leak.

title: GTA 6 Has A Technical Problem And Rockstar Can’t Seem To Fix It
author: Aaron Trueman
content:
There’s a technical issue with GTA 6 and it’s probably not going to be fixed for when the game launches on November 19th. We’ll be delving into this problem and why we won’t see it resolved.
Hold on, before anyone gets upset this is something fans like myself want to talk about because we care about the game. We are big fans of what Rockstar have been able to achieve. How the game performs and feels in the hand is an important part of great video games. There is just one real problem with the game from all the footage we have seen so far.
What’s The Matter?
GTA 6 has an animation/camera pacing issue. As explained by technical experts Digital Foundry, even though the game’s frame rate is a rock solid 30FPS, there is an uneven motion when the camera pans or our main characters move. It can occur in both cut scenes as well as gameplay. Once you see it you can’t unsee it.
In gameplay it’s most noticeable when you don’t pan the camera fast. An example given is during Jason’s walk into the club from the extended look. Whoever is playing was smoothly moving the thumbstick and yet the camera does not look like it is. The issue is subtle but it does give the game a sub-30 FPS look to it even though the the game is actually hitting its frame time perfectly.
This Is Not New
Now I know what some people will be thinking “the game isn’t complete yet”, “we’re only in August and the game releases in November”, “Rockstar will fix it because we can all see it”. Except this has been a problem for Rockstar’s past titles too.
GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 suffer from this issue too. Even their PC versions including the most recent “Enhanced” edition of GTA V. Higher frame rates don’t fix this either so a mythical 60FPS mode for Grand Theft Auto VI will not put an end to it. Digital Foundry speculates that given this issue plaguing past titles and now GTA VI, it is a fundamental issue with RAGE, Rockstar’s engine.
“This may stem from a fundamental timing or synchronisation mismatch between animation and frame updates and it seems unlikely to be resolved for launch given its long history in Rockstar projects.”
Digital Foundry
Why It Probably Won’t Be Fixed
![](https://rockstarintel.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/pMqIk2VptF6gPNPZ-copy.webp)
This issue can be seen in trailer 1, trailer 2 and throughout the recent extended look. All three of these pieces of video were taken from across multiple years at various points in development. GTA 6 is now in its final stage of production. Yes, we are still a few months away from release but if has not been fixed in the past dozen years will it really be fixed in the next few months? Come on, let’s be a realistic now.
Rockstar no doubt know about this technical issue. They have some of the smartest people around working on this game and the engine. As we’ve seen from everything of GTA 6 so far, they are doing things that no one else are able to do on the technical side of video games. Based on this, the issue is not an easy one to solve. They are not careless.
It’s just extremely disappointing that there is this lingering problem that has spanned generations of hardware and games. With Grand Theft Auto VI marking a truly revolutionary step forward in interactive entertainment, it just feels wrong to see an issue like this from the XBOX 360/PS3 era crop up again.
It’s also worth noting that this is not something only Rockstar has suffered from. Other games on different engines have exhibited issues like this before. The difference is Rockstar has effectively an unlimited budget and as I mentioned some of the most clever people in the industry.
Again, this one problem does not take away from the the incredible artistry that has gone into creating this game. Grand Theft Auto 6 is going to be a revolutionary game even if this one RAGE quirk was not fixed.
You can pre-order your PS5 or XBOX copy with this link. Using the link to pre-order the game will help support this website as we’ll earn a small commission. Thank you!
For more news on GTA VI, stay tuned to RockstarINTEL and sign up to our newsletter for a weekly round-up of all things Rockstar Games delivered straight to your inbox.

Subscribe to our newsletter!
summary: Technical analysis by Digital Foundry reveals that Grand Theft Auto 6 suffers from an animation and camera pacing issue that creates uneven motion despite a solid 30FPS frame rate. This subtle glitch causes gameplay and cutscenes to look like they are running below 30FPS during slow camera pans or character movements. Because past Rockstar titles like GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 experienced the same problem, experts believe it is a fundamental flaw in the RAGE engine that is unlikely to be fixed by the November 19th launch.
key_points: GTA 6 features an animation and camera pacing issue that causes uneven motion during slow pans and character movements.
The issue persists despite the game maintaining a solid 30FPS frame rate and perfect frame times.
Similar animation and timing problems have affected past Rockstar titles, including GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2, across multiple hardware generations.
Experts speculate the glitch stems from a fundamental timing or synchronization mismatch within Rockstar's RAGE engine.
The issue is visible across multiple trailers and development builds, making a fix before the November launch unlikely.

title: Solar storms could expose travellers 'a month's worth of radiation in one hour'
author: Josh Milton
content:
![Young Traveler Woman Looking through Airplane Window, Enjoying View](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308726073-d427.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Most people board planes to get away to somewhere hot and sunny – but they might be exposed to the wrong kind of sunshine.
University of Surrey researchers have found that solar storms could expose airline passengers and crew to dangerous amounts of radiation.
The team’s study, published in the Journal of Space Weather and Space Climate, found radiation surges at typical flight altitudes.
‘Cosmic radiation at 40,000 feet is around 300 times higher than at sea level, giving a steady radiation drizzle,’ Professor Clive Dyer, a visiting professor at the Surrey Space Centre and co-author of the study, tells Metro.
‘Solar storms, however, can produce sudden downpours, potentially delivering a month’s worth of this normal cosmic radiation in just one hour.’
Wait, what’s space weather?
![The England team arriving by plane at Birmingham Airport following their third place finish at the FIFA World Cup 2026. Picture date: Sunday July 19, 2026. PA Photo. Photo credit should read: Cody Froggatt/PA Wire. RESTRICTIONS: Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder.](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/SEI_305732241-7339.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
Space weather doesn’t mean rain clouds drifting through the cosmos and that you’d need an umbrella for a moonwalk.
Rather, it describes the angry-looking things the sun does, like blowing chunks of its outer layers at us, called coronal mass ejections.
Then there’s solar wind, the million-miles-per-hour stream of particles it’s constantly spewing.
If both weren’t bad enough, the Earth is also being splattered with cosmic radiation from exploding stars.
‘These variations, particularly those from the sun, can influence life and technology on Earth and are what we call space weather,’ says Professor Dyer.
We don’t need to worry about space weather much, as the Earth’s invisible shield, the magnetic field, keeps us safe.
![](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/coverimages55743081-e8f4.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
The closer to the ground, the less cosmic radiation we’re exposed to. At 40,000 feet, that protection is one-third.
‘Long-haul aircrew typically receive around double the radiation exposure of someone at ground level for every year of flying and some frequent fliers spend even more time in the air,’ says Professor Dyer.
Less protection can be bad news when powerful coronal mass ejections hit the Earth, which cause solar storms.
Also called geomagnetic storms, they can endanger spacecraft, fry power grids and, more pleasantly, illuminate the skies with the Northern Lights.
They won’t cause all the plane cabin lights to switch off or the controls to smoke but will cause minor electronic errors, Single Event Upsets (SEUs).
Last year, aircraft-maker Airbus grounded 6,000 A320 planes after intense solar radiation messed with the flight control computer.
![A view of the total eclipse, as the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun, as seen from on board the Ambassador cruise ship Ambition, off the coast of Greenland. Picture date: Wednesday August 12, 2026. PA Photo. Photo credit should read: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_308089365-ca4b.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646) 
The issue was discovered after a JetBlue flight from Cancún, Mexico, to Newark, US, was forced to make an emergency landing in October 2025.
The plane ‘experienced an altitude drop’ during the flight, the airline said, injuring several passengers.
If that’s minor, what could extreme space weather do?
Severe solar storms are rare, happening every few years. Professor Dyer says one of the most extreme was on February 23, 1956.
If a plane flew at 40,000 feet that day, crew and passengers would have been blanketed with 1,000 times more radiation than normal.
‘The cancer risk from flying through an event of this scale could be around one in 1,000,’ Professor Dyer says, or about ‘a year’s worth of normal flight-related radiation in a single flight’.
‘For people, the concern is an increased cancer risk, while high radiation levels can also disrupt the electronics controlling aircraft.’
It’s been quiet on the solar front since then, but three CMEs collided with the Earth and caused a six-hour-long geomagnetic storm last November.
![](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/solar-flare-d8cf.gif?w=646) 
The solar storm caused radiation to jump to almost 10 times normal high-altitude flight conditions, according to calculations by the SSC.
Despite being just 2% as strong as the 1956 episode, Professor Dyer says it ‘still produced significant radiation levels and indirectly led to aircraft being grounded and fixes being made’.
‘It is a reminder that rare events will happen.’
Researchers say that this doesn’t mean you should cancel your next holiday, but aviation officials need to account more for space weather.
Once a CME happens, we can forecast when it will hit Earth days before.
Air travel can be safer by integrating these forecasts into flight planning, akin to pilots watching the weather report for wind and rain.
- 
	![Karen Cassidy and her husband George Gale waiting in an airport.](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/SEI_309878439-92e7.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&w=646&h=363&crop=1)
- Dog walker 'distressed' after seeing man put carrot up his bum at nature reserve
- Man ends up with £2,000 bill for £250 steak dinner after trying to dine and dash
- Man died after sign reading 'Everything's Unmissable' collapsed at Christian festival
An aviation-specific radiation scale could be introduced, so air traffic control knows if a plane needs to reroute or ground.
Polar flights, which shave off travel time by flying over the North Pole, are vulnerable to extreme solar storms because the magnetic field is weaker at the poles. Such a route could be London Heathrow to Vancouver International, Canada.
‘We have been working on this problem for around 40 years, with significant progress made over the last decade as the dangers of space weather have become more widely recognised,’ adds Professor Dyer.
‘For individuals, the chance of being caught in an extreme event is low, but with growing air traffic, the hazard must be addressed.’
Get in touch with our news team by emailing us at webnews@metro.co.uk.
For more stories like this, check our news page.
summary: Researchers from the University of Surrey have found that solar storms can expose airline passengers and crew to dangerous levels of radiation at typical flight altitudes. While normal cosmic radiation at 40,000 feet is already significantly higher than at sea level, solar storms can deliver a month's worth of radiation in just one hour. These space weather events can also cause minor electronic errors in aircraft, leading experts to suggest that aviation officials should integrate space weather forecasts into flight planning.
key_points: Solar storms can potentially deliver a month's worth of normal cosmic radiation to airline passengers and crew in just one hour.
Radiation from space weather can disrupt aircraft electronics and has previously led to planes being grounded or making emergency landings.
Extreme solar storms can increase cancer risks for individuals flying through them and pose greater vulnerabilities for polar flights.
Researchers suggest that integrating space weather forecasts into flight planning and introducing aviation-specific radiation scales can make air travel safer.

title: Apple will be launching its first pair of smart glasses next year: Here's what's coming - 9to5Mac
author: Michael Burkhardt
content:
![Apple Glasses](https://9to5mac.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2026/04/apple-glasses-02.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600) 
As soon as next year, Apple will be debuting its first pair of AI-powered smart glasses. They’ll integrate Visual Intelligence and bring Siri to the real world. Here’s what we’re expecting.
Core features
First and foremost, these glasses are AI glasses, not AR glasses. That means they’ll primarily be voice and camera-based, as they won’t have any displays.
The cameras will allow Siri to look at your real world environment and answer questions, provide context, and translate signage. Another feature that we’ll likely see on these glasses is the ability for you to ask Siri to save an image of something and remind you later, as we first saw in the macOS 26.7 leak.
They’ll also offer speakers for music and audio playback, so you can think of them as open-ear headphones.
On the other hand, though – they might not allow for the glasses to take photos and videos normally, per Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. Meta’s Ray-Ban glasses have become a massive privacy concern lately, and Apple may want to avoid that.
Styles
Unlike Meta, Apple isn’t partnering with an existing eyewear-maker to design these glasses. According to Bloomberg, the company is instead designing them in house, with a number of different styles in the works:
- A large rectangular frame, reminiscent of Ray-Ban Wayfarers
- A slimmer rectangular design, similar to the glasses worn by Apple Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook
- Larger oval or circular frames
- A smaller, more refined oval or circular option
They’re supposedly going to be made of acetate, a more durable and higher-end alternative to plastic. Apple will also offer them in a few finishes, including black, ocean blue, and light brown.
Health
In a future iteration of the product, Apple is reportedly considering positioning the product as a health device. This could mean they’ll integrate heart-rate monitors (similar to AirPods Pro 3), and it could mean there’ll be additional software features (like Workout Buddy from Apple Watch) to make it more helpful.
Beyond that, it’s unclear how Apple will make these useful for health – just don’t expect it in the first iteration.
Release date
Recent reporting suggests that Apple will unveil these glasses at WWDC 2027 to allow developers to prepare for them. Then, they’ll ship later that year. In all likelihood that’ll mean a September debut, alongside the 20th anniversary all-glass iPhone. You can learn more about that here.
Are you excited for Apple’s first pair of smart glasses? Let us know in the comments.

The in-house designed acetate frames will come in multiple styles and finishes, though standard photo and video capture might be omitted due to privacy concerns. Apple is designing the acetate frames entirely in-house across various rectangular and circular styles.
