title: Gamescom 2026: Classic remakes and new worlds at gaming's biggest showcase
author: Laura Cress
content:
Watch: BBC's Laura Cress on the floor at Gamescom in Cologne
- Published
Gamescom is the largest in-person gaming event in the world, and this year it lived up to expectations with big games on show from The Witcher 3's new expansion, to Alien: Isolation 2.
Last year over 350,000 people flocked to the halls of the Koelnmesse in Cologne, Germany to get a chance to see and play the most hotly anticipated games.
This year that number of attendees is expected to have been even bigger, with the likes of Xbox and Sega showcasing games to the public alongside indie studios with only one or two developers.
This was my sixth time attending Gamescom, which never fails to make me excited about the games industry. Here are a few of the big things I got to check out this week.
The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past
![An in-game screenshot of Witcher 3 showing Geralt with white hair and a red scar across his face, in chainmail](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1680/cpsprodpb/e644/live/028c1140-a285-11f1-ae59-c1f7c17a8b7d.png)
Gamers will once again play as the gruff-voiced Geralt of Rivera in the new The Witcher 3 expansion
When CD Projekt Red announced it was making a new expansion for the hugely popular action-role playing game The Witcher 3, it came as a shock.
The original, after all, came out 11 years ago.
Yet it was clear sitting in the crowd for Opening Night Live on Tuesday that there's still a lot of love for the older game. There were gasps and audible shouts of joy when the team announced they were providing a free upgrade to the original.
As for the expansion, Songs of the Past will follow the gruff-voiced protagonist Geralt in an adventure discovering more about the past of his close friend Dandelion.
Doug Cockle, who voices Geralt, told me it was a "thrill" to return as The Witcher.
"I love this character so much...it's like slipping into a warm bath, or putting on an old pair of shoes," he said.
![Doug Cockle, who plays Geralt, out of his Witcher uniform, alongside Laura Cress](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/562c/live/06d599e0-a219-11f1-9090-b51af3a01fc2.jpg)
Doug Cockle, who plays Geralt, out of his Witcher uniform, alongside Laura Cress
From what I got to see, it's clear choice will once again be front and centre of the player's experience, with lots of options to choose from in how to react to people.
For those hoping to take their time tossing a coin to their Witcher, the head of co-developer Fool's Theory Jakub Rokosz told me this expansion would be "on par with the size" of previous additions such as Blood and Wine and Hearts of Stone.
Alien: Isolation 2
Alien: Isolation 2 is the long-awaited sequel to Horsham-based Creative Assembly's 2014 survival-horror game.
One of the things that made the original Alien: Isolation so terrifying was its seemingly intelligent Xenomorph, which appeared to learn from your behaviour and adapt to it.
Considering I physically jumped out of my seat at one point playing the demo when avoiding the Alien, it's safe to say Creative Assembly will once again be ratcheting up the tension with the sequel.
This time rather than playing as the daughter of Ellen Ripley, you play as Blake, a chief executive of the infamous Weyland-Yutani corporation.
![A close-up in-game screenshot of the Alien](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/736/cpsprodpb/14e9/live/bc3abf00-a286-11f1-91e4-a534e1a56752.jpg)
The Alien is as horrifying as ever
As well as claustrophobic spaceship corridors, in the sequel you will also be avoiding the Alien in bigger, open air spaces.
But the game's Project Art Director Anastasia Sopikova said that did not mean you would always feel safer.
"You step outside. And you're like, 'Oh yeah, I'm relieved, I'm outside," she said.
"And then the rain picks up and it gets foggier, and you hear something nearby and you're like, 'Oh, okay.' Suddenly you realise you're really vulnerable. You're really exposed."
Fable
Ralph Fulton, the founder of Leamington Spa-based Playground Games, told me the 2027 reboot of the role-playing classic Fable had "two tonal pillars" - "Britishness" and "fairy tales".
Fulton said the team was keen to avoid the generic English accents often heard in fantasy games, pointing out that "accent is such an identifier in the UK, where accents change every 15 to 20 miles".
Instead, Fable features voices from across the UK, and a voice cast of over 100 actors.
"I want to hear people from Newcastle, from Edinburgh, from Cardiff, you know? And we've done that and it brings this incredible sense of Britishness, and also this incredible sense of humour," he said.
The game is deliberately not a continuation of the original trilogy's timeline, but it will have some of its quirks, taking players into a new open-world version of Albion - the game's fairy-tale version of medieval Britain.
Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis
Lara Croft has been exploring ancient ruins and culling the local wildlife for nearly 30 years now (the original Tomb Raider came out in 1996).
Legacy of Atlantis revisits Lara's original adventure, including her journey through Peru.
It's not the first time the classic game has been remade, but Jeff Adams, experience director at co-developers Crystal Dynamics, told me reimagining it was still a "very delicate formula".
"You have to be very intentful with where you make modifications, but you do so in the attempt to kind of bring it into a modern gameplay space."
As for why after 30 years people still want to play as the twin-pistoled adventurer, MichaÅ Kuk, Creative Director at Flying Wild Hog, said it was not just about her athletic ability.
"It's also about the attitude, the energy, the self-confidence," he added.
![A giant creature opens its mouth in the Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis booth of the expo](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1440/cpsprodpb/3472/live/50e50af0-a22a-11f1-bd6a-3d72a7f54a3e.jpg)
They went all out with the Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis booth this year
Elsewhere at the expo, over three days some got to take part in an event called Games Done Quick (GDQ), where people try to finish a game as quickly as possible.
Its previous events are often watched by hundreds of thousands of people online, with GDQ's charity marathons having raised "62 million dollars for charities in the last 16 years", according to business director Ashley Farkas.
"Anybody can be a part of this community, anybody can be a speedrunner, and it is just like a giant hug from gamers of like, hey, we want you to come, hang out and do fun stuff and raise money for charity," she said.
Silent Hill Townfall
Silent Hill, the psychological survival horror franchise from Japanese studio Konami, has for the most part been set in America, although the most recent excursion - Silent Hill f - was based in Japan in the 1960s era.
Now in Silent Hill Townfall, made by the Glasgow-based team Screen Burn, that location is in an entirely new place - Scotland, albeit a fictional part of it - St Amelia.
![Laura sits with a person wearing a Silent Hill t-shirt and jacket. Behind them, a creepy sign reading Welcome to St. Amelia - a mock-up of something from the game itself.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1200/cpsprodpb/57ae/live/da7aeff0-a2bb-11f1-9024-715001d09aeb.jpg)
Silent Hill's director says the game's setting is very Scottish
Scotland was initially going to be more of an influence than a setting, but the team ultimately decided to embrace it fully.
Director Jon McKellan told me that approach felt "more natural and kind of authentic", with the game filled with recognisably Scottish shops and signage.
"It's very, very Scottish," he said.
![A green promotional banner with black squares and rectangles forming pixels, moving in from the right. The text says: âTech Decoded: The worldâs biggest tech news in your inbox every Monday.â](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/41d3/live/348b21e0-26a8-11f0-8f57-b7237f6a66e6.png)
summary: Gamescom 2026 drew massive crowds to Cologne, Germany, showcasing major titles ranging from indie projects to blockbusters by Xbox and Sega. The event highlighted several high-profile games, including expansions and remakes like The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, alongside new entries such as Alien: Isolation 2. Developers also shared insights on upcoming titles like the Fable reboot and the Scottish-set Silent Hill Townfall.
key_points: Gamescom is the world's largest in-person gaming event, held annually at the Koelnmesse in Cologne, Germany.
The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past is a new expansion comparable in size to previous additions like Blood and Wine.
Alien: Isolation 2 features protagonist Blake and introduces larger, open-air spaces alongside claustrophobic corridors.
The 2027 Fable reboot focuses on Britishness and fairy tales, utilizing a voice cast of over 100 actors from across the UK.
Silent Hill Townfall is set in a fictional part of Scotland called St Amelia, bringing an authentic Scottish atmosphere to the survival horror franchise.

title: 'This Looks Like Dogsh*t': Disturbing DLSS 5 AI Filter Applied to Major PS5 Games After Leaking
author: Push Square; Sammy Barker
content:
!['This Looks Like Dogsh*t': Disturbing DLSS 5 AI Filter Added to Every Major PS5 Game After Leaking 1](https://images.pushsquare.com/51d6d8a618495/this-looks-like-dogsht-disturbing-dlss-5-ai-filter-added-to-every-major-ps5-game-after-leaking-1.900x.jpg)
Nvidia’s controversial new DLSS 5 filter, which caused a bit of a hullabaloo earlier this year, has leaked online – and instantly been implemented into pretty much every major PS5 game on the market.
While previous iterations of Nvidia’s upscaling technology have broadly been praised – using reconstruction techniques to reduce computational load without impacting image quality – this version appears to use generative AI to alter artistic intent.
This was best observed with an example of Resident Evil Requiem’s Grace Ashcroft earlier in the year, with fans complaining the scaredy-cat heroine had been “yassified”.
And now a version of the technology’s files have been pulled from the PC version of NBA 2K27, which has prompted fans to inject it into a variety of different titles – including many of Sony’s biggest franchises, via their Steam ports.
For example, MJ from Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 looks transformed, with bright red lips and darker coloured eyes.
While she’s still recognisable, it strips away the artistic intent of the original model – regardless of whether you like Insomniac’s take on the character or not.
I personally don’t think this Ellie example is the worst I’ve seen, although she looks years and years older than she’s supposed to and the lighting doesn’t properly match the scene:
And then we have this now infamous example of Cloud from Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth, which borders on parody really:
Nvidia, for the record, says critics are wrong about DLSS 5.
CEO Jensen Huang defended the technology, saying it “doesn't change the artistic control”.
He said: “This is very different than generative AI; it’s content-control generative AI. That’s why we call it neural rendering.”
summary: Nvidia's leaked DLSS 5 filter files from NBA 2K27 have been used by fans to modify major PlayStation games and their Steam ports. Unlike previous praised versions, this iteration appears to use generative AI to alter character models and artistic intent, drawing criticism from fans. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang defended the technology, stating it uses content-control generative AI known as neural rendering and does not alter artistic control.
key_points: Nvidia's controversial DLSS 5 filter files leaked online from the PC version of NBA 2K27.
Fans have injected the technology into major PlayStation games and PC ports, altering character appearances.
Critics argue the filter strips away the original artistic intent of characters like MJ, Ellie, and Cloud.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang defended DLSS 5, asserting it uses content-control generative AI called neural rendering rather than changing artistic control.

title: $900 PS5 Pro Selling Out During PlayStation Blackout Amid GTA 6 Fever
author: Push Square; Sammy Barker
content:
![$900 PS5 Pro Selling Out During PlayStation Blackout Amid GTA 6 Fever 1](https://images.pushsquare.com/01df7d077eea0/usd900-ps5-pro-selling-out-during-playstation-blackout-amid-gta-6-fever-1.900x.jpg)
Sony’s supercharged PS5 Pro hardware model is selling out in the US as GTA 6 fever takes hold – despite an ongoing blackout protest taking place against PlayStation hardware.
Fans have mobilised to keep their consoles unplugged indefinitely, but such is the demand for the PS5’s most powerful model that third-party sellers are charging as much as $1,300 for the device on Amazon. That’s a huge mark-up on its $900 MSRP.
Stores like Best Buy and Target are also out of stock, although the former is flogging “open box” units just below MSRP.
You can also still get a brand new model through PS Direct, with no mark-up or hidden expenses.
GTA 6 has been described by tech experts as the “most impressive example of real-time rendering we’ve ever seen”, and while a 60fps option looks unlikely, many want to enjoy it in the best condition possible.
PS5 Pro is currently the most powerful console on the market, and Rockstar has said all along that the game will “play best” on Sony’s devices, as it’s the lead platform for the game.
summary: Sony's $900 PS5 Pro is selling out across major US retailers like Best Buy and Target amid high demand driven by anticipation for GTA 6. Despite an ongoing fan blackout protest keeping some consoles unplugged, third-party sellers on Amazon are charging up to $1,300 for the device. Brand new models remain available at standard retail price through PS Direct, while Rockstar has stated that GTA 6 will play best on Sony's hardware.
key_points: The $900 PS5 Pro is currently selling out at major US retailers including Best Buy and Target.
Third-party sellers on Amazon are marking up the console price to as much as $1,300.
Brand new PS5 Pro models can still be purchased without a mark-up directly through PS Direct.
High demand for the console is fueled by anticipation for GTA 6, which Rockstar confirmed will run best on Sony devices.

title: GTA 6's gameplay reveal broke a streaming record, and also broke Twitch and Netflix
author: Vikki Blake
content:
Reaction streams to Grand Theft Auto 6's first gameplay presentation peaked at 3,970,738 viewers across livestreaming platforms, making it the biggest gaming stream of 2026 so far.
That's according to new data from Streams Charts, which claims 9,038 streamers covered Rockstar Games' Netflix reveal, racking up 5,227,798 hours watched.
That puts GTA 6's reveal ahead of Summer Game Fest 2026's 3.81 million peak viewers, as well as June's Nintendo Direct and State of Play broadcasts. Twitch carried the largest share of the audience, accounting for around 44 percent of total hours watched, ahead of YouTube (34.8% percent) and Kick (20.2 percent).
Spanish streamer Juan Alberto "IlloJuan" García led the way with 233,520 peak viewers, a new record for his own channel, ahead of Rubius (191,056) and IShowSpeed (177,887).
The reveal went out at 8pm UK time, but heavy demand caused technical issues on both Netflix and Twitch, with some viewers reportedly locked out for 40-50 minutes. That didn't deter internet hype, though; Streams Charts also tracked more than 100,000 chat messages about the game across the three-hour window it analysed.
While the bulk of tracked messages about the reveal – 65-72 percent – were neutral, positive messages made up 11-15 percent of the total, while negative messages sat at around 17-20 percent, much of it aimed at the Twitch and Netflix outages rather than the game itself.
Around a fifth of all messages also compared the reveal to Grand Theft Auto 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2, generally with a negative tone, with one viewer complaining: "GTA V DLC FOR 80$ LMAO".
Cloudflare, which handles more than a fifth of global internet traffic, has since shared its own numbers on the reveal's ripple effects. Netflix's global traffic rose 16 percent compared to previous weeks as the Extended Look aired, with the spike even sharper in the UK at 45 percent.
Twitch saw its own surge, averaging a 12 percent increase over the three hours following the premiere and peaking at 35 percent, while YouTube jumped 39 percent when the trailer went live there at 1am.
But it was Rockstar's own website that saw the biggest swing of all, with traffic climbing 172 percent worldwide and a huge 1210 percent in the UK.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is due out on November 19th for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. This week's GTA 6 bonanza revealed a wealth of new information about the game, such as a changed Wanted system, a changed carjacking system, a new romance system, a huge game world, and a list of in-game activities.
This is what a billion dollars gets you, observed Chris Donlan, though as Chris Tapsell pointed out, this push towards realism and away from easy-going fun is a huge risk for the series – even if, he argued, it's ultimately right that it takes it.
It's a big and exciting moment for Rockstar after a week of leaked GTA 6 videos. But the hype has a bitter edge, as dozens of employees recently fired by Rockstar North continue to battle the company in employment tribunals over alleged union-busting.
summary: The first gameplay presentation for Grand Theft Auto 6 broke streaming records by peaking at nearly 4 million viewers across platforms, surpassing other major 2026 gaming broadcasts. Heavy viewer demand caused temporary outages on Twitch and Netflix, while web traffic surged globally for the streaming services and Rockstar's website. The game is scheduled for release on November 19th for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.
key_points: GTA 6's gameplay reveal peaked at 3,970,738 viewers, making it the biggest gaming stream of 2026 so far.
Twitch accounted for the largest share of watch time at 44 percent, followed by YouTube at 34.8 percent and Kick at 20.2 percent.
Heavy demand caused technical outages on both Twitch and Netflix, locking some viewers out for 40 to 50 minutes.
Rockstar's website experienced a massive 172 percent increase in worldwide traffic and a 1210 percent spike in the UK.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is set to launch on November 19th for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

title: DLSS 5 Patched to Work on RTX 4000 "Ada Lovelace" GPUs Despite No Official Support
author: DrUsmanSaleem Discuss
content:
Friday, August 28th 2026
	
		
![NVIDIA](https://tpucdn.com/images/news/nvidia-v1788010518.png) 
The modding community has been hard at work ever since the untimely release of DLSS-NR, a precursor to DLSS 5. Now, modders have gotten NVIDIA's leaked DLSS 5 tool working on RTX 4000 series cards, even though the tool was only built for RTX 5000 Blackwell hardware. The DLL leaked earlier this week via an early-access build of NBA 2K27, and people on the RenoDX Discord quickly got it running in other games using ReShade and RenoDX.
As we noted in our DLSS-NR breakdown, the AI model runs on FP8, which Ada Lovelace GPUs support just fine, but the compiled binaries inside the file only targeted Blackwell's sm_120 architecture, with nothing built for Ampere or Ada. A modder going by "Uncle Burrito" has apparently fixed that by hunting down the incompatible binaries and swapping in ones built for Ada. Tom's Hardware confirmed the patch works on an RTX 4080, and said other developers in the same Discord are working on their own versions of the fix.
![](https://tpucdn.com/img/cFxxKlXUNA2hUdg1_thm.jpg) It's still early and rough around the edges, and there's no word yet on whether NVIDIA plans to officially support older cards at launch. However, given how quickly modders cracked this open, it looks like NVIDIA may have little choice but to consider it. Older cards like Ampere could be a tougher case though, since they lack native FP8 support altogether.

				Uncle Burrito on YouTube, 				Tom's Hardware

summary: Modders have successfully patched NVIDIA's leaked DLSS 5 tool to function on RTX 4000 "Ada Lovelace" graphics cards, despite the software officially targeting only RTX 5000 Blackwell hardware. The leak originated from an early-access build of NBA 2K27, prompting modders to swap incompatible binaries for Ada-compatible ones. While confirmed to work on an RTX 4080, it remains uncertain if NVIDIA will officially extend support to older hardware generations.
key_points: A leaked DLSS 5 DLL file, originally built exclusively for Blackwell architecture, was cracked by the modding community.
A modder named "Uncle Burrito" fixed the architecture incompatibility by swapping binaries to support Ada Lovelace GPUs.
Tom's Hardware confirmed the resulting patch successfully operates on an RTX 4080.
Older Ampere cards may struggle to receive official support because they lack native FP8 hardware capabilities.

title: How to watch Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra launch live
author: Diane Templado
content:
Apple’s next big iPhone event is almost here, with the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Ultra, all expected to make their debut.
The event will also mark the first major Apple product launch since John Ternus takes over as CEO on September 1. As with recent launches, Apple will combine an in-person gathering at Apple Park with a prerecorded presentation.
When is the iPhone 18 Pro/Ultra event?
The event will take place on Wednesday, September 9, starting at 10am PDT (1pm EDT). For other regions, the event starts at 6pm BST in the UK, 7pm CEST in Central Europe and 10:30pm IST in India. Viewers in China can tune in at 1am CST on September 10, followed by 2am JST in Japan and 3am AEST in Sydney.
Apple’s official event page also includes an Add to Calendar option, which automatically adjusts the event time for your location. It’s worth opening the stream a few minutes early, particularly if you want to catch the opening announcements.
How can I watch the event?
The simplest option is to watch through Apple’s official event website using Safari or another web browser. The stream is free, and you don’t need an Apple TV+ subscription to watch it. You can also use the Apple TV app on supported Apple devices.
If you have an Apple TV 4K, open the TV app and look for the event on the Home screen. If it doesn’t appear immediately, you can search for the event or open Apple’s website using another device. There’s also the option of watching on a larger screen with AirPlay. To do this, start the stream on an iPhone, iPad or Mac and send it to an Apple TV 4K or compatible smart TV. The devices must be connected to the same Wi-Fi network.
Windows PC and Android users aren’t left out. You can watch the presentation directly through Apple’s website or use the official YouTube livestream. The YouTube listing is already available, and selecting Set Reminder will send you a notification when the event begins.
If you miss the live presentation, Apple will make a replay available through its event website and Apple TV app. The YouTube stream will remain available too, so you can catch up later.
What will be announced?
The headline products should be the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Ultra, with the latter potentially being Apple’s biggest iPhone change in years. The iPhone Ultra is expected to be Apple’s first foldable iPhone. Therefore, it puts the device directly into competition with foldable phones that Samsung, Google and other manufacturers have been producing for years.
Apple isn’t expected to unveil the entire iPhone 18 range at this event. The standard iPhone 18 is reportedly part of Apple’s new split launch strategy and should arrive later. This leaves September’s event focused on the company’s premium models.
The Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are also expected to join the new iPhones. Together, these will round out Apple’s usual autumn hardware refresh.
summary: Apple is set to host a product launch event on Wednesday, September 9, featuring the debut of the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the foldable iPhone Ultra. This event marks the first major product launch under incoming CEO John Ternus. Viewers can watch the livestream for free via Apple's official website, the Apple TV app, or YouTube.
key_points: The event takes place on Wednesday, September 9, starting at 10am PDT.
Expected hardware announcements include the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the foldable iPhone Ultra.
Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 are also expected to be unveiled.
The livestream is free and accessible via Apple's website, the Apple TV app, and YouTube.

title: Existing Garmin Watches Will Get Fenix 9 Features: Here's the Full Details!
author: Ray Maker
content:
![Youtube video](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/GX8nW1l8S-I/hqdefault.jpg)
The changes to the Fenix 9 series are most easily grouped into two buckets: Hardware changes and Software changes. While this has always been true in the past, the biggest change here is that, unlike past generational leaps where Garmin ditched the existing models for software updates, the Fenix 9 doesn’t make that ditch. Instead, all existing Fenix 8 series devices will get virtually all the software updates (minus a few that are hardware-dependent). Even further, those changes will also go to the majority of same-platform non-Fenix watches too, such as the Forerunner 970, Venu X1, Forerunner 570, and many more within the newer common GarminOS (semi-official name) platform.
Now, I’ll have plenty more Fenix 9 details over the next while…once I untangle the giant box of Fenix 9 units that’s been stuck in customs jail for a while. Win some, lose some….
The Software Changes:
![FieldTools.jpg](https://media.dcrainmaker.com/images/2026/08/FieldTools.jpg)
When it comes to new software features, as noted above, virtually all of these are coming to the Fenix 8 series, Enduro 3, Tactix 8, as well as Forerunner 970/570, Fenix E, and Venu X1 series. A portion of them also to the Venu 4, Vivoactive 6, and other features further to other ‘new platform’ devices. As a quick reminder, last summer (2025) leading up to the Fenix 8 Pro launch, Garmin consolidated their software platform behind the scenes. While each brand has slight user interface (visual) differences/stylings, the codebase is now consolidated. That’s resulted in virtually all watches on the platform getting virtually all new features (save some saved for higher-end devices).
Historically though, each time Garmin ‘jumped’ a model version, it would ditch the old one. For example, Fenix 6 devices didn’t get Fenix 7 or Fenix 7 Pro features. Fenix 7/7Pro devices didn’t get new Fenix 8 or Fenix 8 Pro features. Within the same numbering, they would, but outside of that, tough luck.
This shift represents a *MASSIVE* change for Garmin. While the dust is still settling, it can’t be overstated enough as to how big a change this is. It means if you have a Fenix 8 watch, you’ll get almost all these features. Same for a Forerunner 970 watch. For something like the Forerunner 570, it’ll get those that are ‘applicable’ to the watch. For example, the Forerunner 570 didn’t do Stamina, so it wouldn’t get the expanded Stamina features. Same goes for mapping things, since it didn’t do mapping.
The only caveat on the Fenix 8, is that it won’t get the items listed in the Mapping sections below. The reason is apparently tied to an entirely new mapping engine under the covers, which is specific to the Fenix 9 series. The Fenix 9 Pro has a newer processor (than the Fenix 9 base), which accounts for further mapping speed increases. Likewise, the re-named satellite battery modes aren’t going to other devices, but honestly I see that as a good thing (more on why later on). And finally, the new archery feature (ArcheryX), won’t go back to other watches.
Finally, there are further features which are lit-up for even earlier watches (via Garmin Connect), such as the Garmin Epic feature, the Endurance Score expansions, Messenger FindMyPeoples update, etc…
Not a single feature here requires Garmin Connect+, which is notable. In any case, diving into all these software-specific changes (both on-device, and via Garmin Connect app):
– Added new Garmin Epic feature, which groups multi-day events/adventures (both on-device, and Garmin Connect)
– New Stamina zone concept (see below, both on-device and on Garmin Connect)
– Added New Stamina Endurance time concept
– Added New Stamina trending feature (on Garmin Connect)
– Added New Running & Cycling Stamina graphs/curves
– Added New Rucking/Pack-Weight calorie breakout for activities (in multiple sport profiles)
– Revamped algorithms around pack-weight, to more accurately cover calorie impacts
– Added New Rucking target calculator on-watch: Can tell you how far you need to go for a certain goal & pack weight
– Added ability to change pack-weight mid-activity
– Added Dedicated Rucking Reports (summarizing pack weight, calories, elevation, pace)
– Added Rucking Multisport mode option
– Added New on-device Rucking structured workouts with GoRuck
– Added New Ski Erg Profile (officially called ‘XC Ski Indoor’)
– Huge update/change for Indoor Rowing
– Added new heart rate zones for rowing, and max heart rate
– Added new power zones and power curves for running
– Added new indoor rowing FTP values/estimation
– Added new indoor rowing VO2Max values
– Added lactate threshold for rowing, and performance condition
– Added indoor rowing activity profile countdown timer (5-second timer, to let you get ready)
– Added support for indoor rowing to update Training Status (e.g., Productive, Unproductive, etc…)
– Added new Garmin Locate feature within Garmin Messenger app
– Added ability to see athlete heart rate, pace, distance, elevation information in Garmin Messenger App
– Added inReach weather updates feature (get weather updates via satellite)
– Added Rolling GAP as a data field (both kilometer and mile)
– Added Rolling GAP as a structured workout target option
– Added new on-device watch face editor (AMOLED-only models)
– Added new ‘Field Tools’ feature, including ABC, measure height, reference point, and more
I outline all of these features in the video up above, one-by-one, on how they all work, and more details on each one. I’ll expand out this post shortly with more photos/etc…stay tuned!
Note that for features like Epic, you can go right now into Garmin Connect Mobile and build that out for past adventures with any watch. I did that today, for my Tour du Mont Blanc adventure in 2022, based on older Garmin Fenix 7, Enduro 2, and Forerunner 955 watches. Only the on-device summary pieces need newer hardware.
Fenix 9 Series Features Only:
![PerspectiveView.jpg](https://media.dcrainmaker.com/images/2026/08/PerspectiveView.jpg)
Now there are a few features that aren’t coming to the earlier units, for slightly different reasons each. Here’s the quick version, and then I’ll explain why:
– Added new Dynamic Battery modes, which basically simplify the naming of the satellite modes
– Removed forced multi-band satellite option (all versions now have a variant of SatIQ)
– Mapping: New Perspective view (sorta a tilted map view)
– Mapping: Smoother/faster zoom
– Mapping: More responsive heading updates (orientation)
– Added new ArcheryX feature
For the mapping-related ones, Garmin says those depend on an entirely new mapping engine on the Fenix 9. That new mapping engine leverages hardware differences on the Fenix 9, including 50% more memory, more storage, plus on the Fenix 9 Pro variant, there’s an entirely new processor. Garmin did note that the differences between the map panning/etc speeds from Fenix 9 base to Fenix 9 Pro aren’t actually that different (the claim is 30-40% faster panning and calculation speeds over the Fenix 8, compared to the Fenix 9 Pro). Meaning the bulk of these speeds are coming from the rewrite, and likely more memory.
As for the new Dynamic battery modes, these are mostly just a renaming of existing modes, and removing the forced multi-band option. Garmin says they’re standardizing all battery claims on all new products going forward on this set of four modes, seen below:
![SatelliteModes.png](https://media.dcrainmaker.com/images/2026/08/SatelliteModes.png)
I get the reason they don’t want to push these battery mode names back to older units, as that would then force them to re-do all the battery claims for every model. Which, I think we can all agree would be a giant pain in the ass. It wouldn’t change the underwritten claims, but rather, just rename the modes slightly. So, fair enough.
As for the ArcheryX feature, well…upsell gonna upsell! That said, I’m OK to let the Robinhood folks take one for the team, with us being the team. Sorry folks, I do still think you’re cool!
Going Forward:
![NewFeatures.jpg](https://media.dcrainmaker.com/images/2026/08/NewFeatures.jpg)
It’s hard to overstate how big a shift this is for Garmin. This is the first time in…well…probably the last 15+ years, where Garmin has brought features back to a different wearable product generation. There were times in the Edge cycling units when features were rolled back to previous generations in certain scenarios, but even then, it wasn’t really seen as a single cohesive product grouping.
Whereas now, Garmin looks at the firmware for these models as a single group: The Fenix 8/8 Pro/9/9Pro/etc variants alongside that of the other ‘modern’ models from the Forerunner and Venu lineups. Obviously, this won’t help Fenix 6 or Fenix 7 users. Nor will it help variants like the Instinct 3 series that are dancing to their own tune. But a *ton* of derivative Garmin models (think Tactix, Approach, etc…) are all based on the newer core GarminOS common operating system.
Point being, myself and many others have given Garmin a pretty hard time on this over the years. Heck, I just shot a Pixel Watch 5 In-Depth Review last night where I gave Garmin a hard time for this. This changes that. But hopefully, it also sticks. Only time will tell.
Speaking of time, there isn’t yet a super-clear public schedule for when the firmware updates to existing devices will roll out. I’m awaiting word whether it’s the very-near-term quarterly maintenance release (which would be any day/week now), or the following one later this fall. I’ll update once I have word. [Update: Got confirmation from Garmin it won’t make this fall’s quarterly release (which is the last one of the year), which means it’d be pushed to early next year likely).]
With that – thanks for reading, and stay tuned for plenty more in-depth testing and thoughts on the Fenix 9 very shortly. Well, UPS willing…

summary: Garmin is breaking from past practices by bringing most new Fenix 9 software features to existing devices on its newer common GarminOS platform, including the Fenix 8 series, Enduro 3, and various Forerunner and Venu models. While older devices will receive updates for features like rucking metrics, indoor rowing profiles, and Garmin Messenger integrations, a few hardware-dependent features will remain exclusive to the Fenix 9 series. These exclusive features include a new mapping engine with perspective view, renamed dynamic battery modes, and the ArcheryX feature. The firmware updates containing these features are expected to roll out to existing devices by early next year.
key_points: Garmin is bringing nearly all Fenix 9 software features to existing Fenix 8 series and other modern platform watches.
Hardware-dependent features such as the new mapping engine, dynamic battery modes, and ArcheryX remain exclusive to the Fenix 9.
New software additions for existing devices include expanded stamina zones, comprehensive rucking metrics, and updated indoor rowing profiles.
The widespread rollout of these firmware updates to existing compatible watches is anticipated for early next year.

title: Apple TV now costs $14.99 a month after its fourth price hike in four years
author: Stevie Bonifield
content:
Apple raised the price of its streaming service for new and current subscribers on Friday, bumping it up from $12.99 per month to $14.99, Deadline and Variety are reporting. An annual subscription now costs $119, up from $99. Apple also increased the cost of its individual Apple One subscription, which includes Apple TV and Apple’s other subscription services, from $19.95 per month to $21.95.
Apple TV now costs $14.99 a month after its fourth price hike in four years
The Apple TV subscription now costs $2 more each month.
![Severance_Photo_021019](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/02/Severance_Photo_021019.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=18.75%2C0%2C62.5%2C100&w=2400)
![Severance_Photo_021019](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/02/Severance_Photo_021019.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=18.75%2C0%2C62.5%2C100&w=2400)
According to Deadline and Variety, the price change is effective immediately, and current subscribers will be notified of it before their next bill.
This price hike comes almost exactly a year after Apple last increased its Apple TV subscription fee. It comes just weeks after Apple premiered the fourth season of Ted Lasso, and has increasingly aired live sports like F1, MLB, and Major League Soccer in addition to its prestige TV shows and original movies. Earlier this year, Apple also raised prices on almost all of its devices, and is reportedly planning to increase AppleCare Plus subscription prices.
summary: Apple has increased the monthly price of its streaming service from $12.99 to $14.99 for both new and current subscribers, marking its fourth price hike in four years. Additionally, the annual subscription rose to $119, and the individual Apple One bundle increased from $19.95 to $21.95 per month. The price adjustments coincide with recent platform content offerings, including the fourth season of Ted Lasso and various live sports.
key_points: Apple TV monthly subscription increased from $12.99 to $14.99.
The annual subscription price rose from $99 to $119.
The individual Apple One subscription increased from $19.95 to $21.95 per month.
This represents the fourth price hike for the streaming service in four years.

title: GTA 6 extended look: What we know after Netflix preview
author: Tom Richardson
content:
![Screenshot from GTA 6 shows Lucia resting her elbows on the corner of a swimming pool next to what appears to be a rooftop hotel bar. A cocktail glass is on her right and a mobile phone on top of a folded towel is on her left.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/956b/live/a59bfb30-a25c-11f1-a291-b542ee92de7c.jpg)
Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the most anticipated video games ever
- Published
After more than 18 months since the last official glimpse of Grand Theft Auto 6, developer Rockstar has shown fans a 26-minute preview of the upcoming blockbuster video game.
Its "extended look" debuted on Netflix, six hours before going live on YouTube, and was the first chance players have had to see detailed footage of the title in action.
The montage, with no commentary or explanatory captions, showed off improved graphics, detailed environments and a selection of car-chases and shoot-outs from the sequel.
The broadcast followed a week of unauthorised gameplay leaks, which the developer said it had been "heartbreaking" to see shared online.
After it got its chance to show the version of GTA 6 it wanted the world to see, here are some things we learned, and some things we still don't know.
Two's company
![A screenshot from GTA 6 shows main characters Lucia and Jason standing back-to-back against a palm tree-lined sunset. She wears tinted glasses, her long dark hair styled in side-parted cornrows. She wears a tan suede jacket over a string bikini top. He also wears tinted shades and a white shirt with an oversized collar and floral pattern.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/bc9d/live/861576b0-9d89-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
Grand Theft Auto 6 follows the story of couple Lucia and Jason
The extended look spent a long time showcasing the relationship between protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Camino, the couple at the centre of GTA 6's "Bonnie and Clyde" story.
In a preview published on website IGN, external, the developers said the characters' story - and the way it unfolds - can be affected by the player's actions, although they can "opt out" of developing the pair's bond if they want.
The Netflix preview didn't show this playing out in detail, but did show the ability to change control between the two characters at different points.
In one segment, Jason was seen lowering Lucia from a window as they escaped from a drug bust in a block of apartments.
A similar switching system was used in Grand Theft Auto 5, which had three playable main characters.
'The best-looking game'
![Two characters from GTA 6 gesture at the viewer. One, wearing a heavy gold watch, pulls back his top lip to reveal teeth covered in gold. The man next to him wears three thick, gold chains, one with a large round medallion attached. Both are heavily tattooed. The image is convincingly lifelike despite being computer generated](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/68fe/live/0161f050-a25d-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
Fans said the detailed characters in the game were "mind-blowing" to see
Praise for GTA 6's graphics was more or less universal, with characters displaying photorealistic faces and lifelike movements.
Fans were also impressed by the detailed locations on show, which included the interiors of apartments, rooftop bars and sleazy underground clubs.
The preview also showcased the various environments of Leonida, the fictional, Florida-inspired US state where GTA 6 is set.
The range of different body shapes and sizes among background characters - something rarely seen in video games - was also highlighted by many players watching online.
Journalist Ryan McCaffrey said GTA 6 "might be the best-looking game I've ever seen".
The impressive visual fidelity has been attributed to the amount of time Rockstar has spent working on the game, and its budget, which is thought to be among the most expensive in video game history.
It's still Grand Theft Auto
![Cal Hampton, a character from GTA 6, stands in front of an alligator-themed crazy golf course. He holds a putter over one shoulder, and pulls a tongue-out face at the viewer. His loud, green, floral shirt stands out against the browns of the golf course. Behind him, a companion can be seen lining up an attempted putt, while a large alligator statue looms over the course.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/8f19/live/7aac83d0-9d8a-11f1-aed2-8d6da8d75094.jpg)
Rockstar's games are renowed for their attention to detail and vast worlds packed with activities
While GTA 6 appears to break new ground in terms of visuals and scale, it is still, at its heart, a Grand Theft Auto game.
During the preview, viewers saw the armed heists, car chases and criminal underworld scenes that have become a trademark of the series.
Satirical swipes at US culture, darkly comic interactions between characters and a huge range of optional side activities were all present once again.
And Rockstar appears to have expanded on features it introduced in its last major release, 2018 hit Red Dead Redemption 2, such as an "honour" system that affects the player's reputation among other characters.
Fans of the series, which is estimated to have sold half a billion copies since it launched in 1997, will have been thrilled to see it.
No news on GTA 6 Online
![A male character from GTA 6 in an open-collared shirt with slicked-back hair and sunglasses leans, arms folded, against the controls of a yacht as it coasts down a waterway flanked by skyscrapers. A road bridge opens in the distance as orange dawn light reflects of the glass fronts of the tall buildings. The computer-generated image is convincingly lifelike.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/ce4f/live/a3eacca0-a147-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.jpg)
The game is set amid the underworld of Leonida, a fictional US state inspired by Florida
Rockstar had already stated that GTA 6 will be a "single-player experience" on launch, leaving fans to assume a follow-up to the incredibly successful online element of its previous games would come later.
The Netflix preview was dedicated to showing off the story and gameplay, and was not necessarily expected to highlight any new multiplayer features.
Although the launch of the game on 19 November is widely expected to be the biggest of all time, the long-term success of GTA 6 will be judged on how well Rockstar converts players to any new online mode.
GTA online, which also launched after the release of GTA 5, remains one of the most-played games in the world, and is thought to have generated billions of dollars for Rockstar.
The previous game in the series, GTA 5, also broke records when it came out in 2013 and has sold more than 200 million copies since.
Two official trailers for the sixth game have almost 500 million combined views on YouTube, and the Netflix "extended look" on Thursday is being marketed as an event by the streaming service.
Next month the company is due to appear at an employment tribunal in Scotland to defend itself against claims it illegally sacked a group of ex-employees for trying to form a union.
It strongly denies the accusations, and says the workers were fired on the grounds of gross misconduct.
Additional reporting by Thomas Fabbri.
![A footer logo for BBC Newsbeat. It has the BBC logo and the word Newsbeat in white over a colorful background of violet, purple and orange shapes. At the bottom a black square reading "Listen on Sounds" is visible.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/976/cpsprodpb/2e16/live/2c659f70-76bd-11f1-9510-1546718f668b.jpg)
summary: Developer Rockstar recently debuted a 26-minute preview of the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 on Netflix, following unauthorized gameplay leaks. The footage showcased the Bonnie and Clyde-style relationship between protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Camino, improved graphics in the fictional state of Leonida, and classic series staples like armed heists and car chases. The game is scheduled to launch as a single-player experience on November 19, with no new details revealed about a future online multiplayer mode.
key_points: Rockstar released a 26-minute extended look of GTA 6 on Netflix before it went live on YouTube.
The game follows a Bonnie and Clyde-style story featuring protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Camino, allowing players to switch control between them.
Viewers and critics praised the game's photorealistic graphics, detailed environments, and varied background character designs set in the fictional state of Leonida.
The preview featured traditional series gameplay elements including armed heists, car chases, satirical humor, and optional side activities.
The game will launch as a single-player experience on November 19, with no details shared regarding a multiplayer online mode.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Launch: Apple Confirms Keynote And Full Schedule Here
author: David Phelan
content:
Updated, Aug, 27: This article, first published on Tuesday, Aug. 25, has been updated with further details of the new iPhone schedule before it goes on sale.
Apple has taken the first public step in a journey that will end when the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and the company’s first foldable, whatever that turns out to be called, goes on sale.
Below are the moments to watch for. And you can read a full run-down of the expected schedule here.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro: Invites Confirmed
Apple has confirmed its September special event. Luckily, it’s on the date I’ve been predicting since May (details below). The keynote was confirmed on Wednesday, Aug. 26, at 10 a.m. Pacific, 1 p.m. Eastern and 6 p.m. U.K.
Apple sent invites to members of the media and special guests, with the cryptic phrase “Surprise and Shine” and an image, which everyone can have fun trying to decode.
That decoding has already begun with Mark Gurman from Bloomberg posting on X: “What I am seeing: - Shining light = mechanical aperture on the iPhone 18 Pro Max - Sky Blue color = Possible new iPhone 18 Pro color.”
Gurman is right to focus on the color as this is almost always something Apple reveals in the invite. And observers have been predicting a blue iPhone 18 Pro.
Often, the invites are more colorful but the expectation is that the iPhone 18, which usually comes in more colors than the Pro versions, will be held until spring 2027, when it will earn its own invite.
I’m less persuaded that the mechanical aperture predicted to be part of the phone’s camera is tipped in the invite. While I believe it will happen, I’m not convinced that is what the graphic is trying to convey.
The invite revealed exactly when and where the iPhone announcement will take place.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro: The Keynote Date Confirmed
Again, as I had thought, the event will be on Wednesday, Sept. 9, exactly two weeks after the invites were sent out. Almost to the minute, in fact, because the keynote will start at 10 a.m. Pacific, 1 p.m. Eastern and 6 p.m. U.K.
There had been rumors that it would be on Tuesday, Sept. 8 but I felt that was impossible: Apple has literally never held an iPhone event on the day after Labor Day. Well, it’s not breaking that tradition now.
It will take place in the Steve Jobs Theater in Apple Park, the company’s Cupertino, California HQ.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro: The Keynote Details Confirmed
Unless there’s a break with tradition, the keynote will last anywhere between one and two hours and is likely to follow a prescribed format.
It will begin with a live introduction from the stage by Apple CEO John Ternus, his first go after he’ll replace Tim Cook on Tuesday, Sept. 1. Cook will become Apple’s executive chairman.
After the introduction, Apple will screen its keynote movie, a high-production-quality affair with special effects and every detail of each new product.
It’s possible there will be more live elements than before, perhaps as a way for Ternus to indicate that things are changing while still showing continuity.
As well as the iPhones, expect the event to reveal two new Apple Watches. There had been rumors of new Macs, but Apple announced them on Tuesday, Aug. 25 — full details here.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro: Pre-Orders Begin (Predicted)
The next date in the calendar after the keynote will be the opening of pre-orders. Usually, this is on the Friday after the keynote.
However, since the Friday in question is Sept. 11, a date Apple has respectfully avoided since 2001, and since this year is the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, it’s believed that the pre-orders will open on Saturday, Sept. 12 instead.
The exact timing, if previous timetables are followed, will be at 5 a.m. Pacific, 8 a.m. Eastern, 1 p.m. U.K.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro: iOS 27 General Release (Predicted)
The new iPhones will come pre-loaded with the next cycle of software, iOS 27 (although that doesn’t rule out the possibility of a day-one update, which has happened several times in recent years).
The most likely date, I believe, will be Monday, Sept. 14, though the following day is also a possibility. As for timing, I’d expect it could be a little earlier in the day than the usual iOS release timing (10 a.m. Pacific). This could be as early as 8 a.m. Pacific, 11 a.m. Eastern, 4 p.m. U.K.
Whatever time it is, please practice patience. There are always huge numbers of people who want to update as soon as they can so Apple’s servers, even with extra capacity laid on, may require a bit of a wait.
Additionally, please note that iPhones from iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max onwards will be able to run Siri AI, and access to this is likely require users to sign up to a waitlist.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro: The On-Sale Date (Predicted)
Unless there’s an upheaval to the timetable, Apple will put the new phones on sale on the Friday of the week after the keynote, which means the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and the first foldable iPhone will land in stores on Friday, Sept. 18.
summary: Apple has confirmed its September special event and sent out media invites featuring the phrase 'Surprise and Shine.' The keynote is scheduled for Wednesday, Sept. 9, at the Steve Jobs Theater, where the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the company's first foldable phone are expected to be unveiled alongside new Apple Watches. John Ternus is set to deliver his first live introduction as Apple CEO following Tim Cook's transition to executive chairman.
key_points: Apple's special event keynote is confirmed for Wednesday, Sept. 9, at the Steve Jobs Theater in Apple Park.
Media invites included the phrase 'Surprise and Shine' alongside speculation about a Sky Blue color and a mechanical aperture.
John Ternus will lead his first introduction as Apple CEO, following Tim Cook becoming executive chairman on Sept. 1.
Pre-orders are predicted to open on Saturday, Sept. 12, to avoid the anniversary of 9/11 on Friday, Sept. 11.
The new devices, including the iPhone 18 Pro series and a foldable model, are predicted to go on sale Friday, Sept. 18.

title: Rockstar Posts Statement On ‘GTA 6’ Leaks As Lucia Story Spoilers Hit
author: Paul Tassi
content:
After more than a week of persistent Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks from a source known as Cyberleeks, Rockstar has issued its first public comment on the situation.
In the post, which racked up 380,000 likes on Twitter in just over an hour, Rockstar calls the situation “heartbreaking for the team” and that it is “obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time." Why now? A number of reasons.
- Rockstar recognizes that actual GTA 6 story spoilers are expected to begin Wednesday, as promised by Cyberleeks, who to date has only shared locations and normal gameplay. There has been a cutscene clip of Lucia at the time of this writing, but more is expected.
- There is no reference to identifying the leaker and stopping the leaks, and as of a few days ago, internal reporting said that Rockstar couldn’t find them and didn’t know how the leak of a playable build happened in the first place.
- After more than a week, this had to be addressed, even if the leaks had not yet been stopped; this could continue indefinitely. The statement also comes one day ahead of the official Netflix gameplay premiere, though at this point, that may show off the same amount of footage as the leaks.
A problem is that GTA 6 is still a full three months away. This is not happening right before launch. There is no telling just how much might end up leaked by the end of all this, though we don’t know the state of the investigation at this point, and Rockstar isn’t sharing that. But the cadence of leaks, which is now as many as three a day, is increasing. 
Even with the gameplay reveal, there’s nothing to say that a lot more won’t be leaked after that, and of course, the threat of story spoilers going forward.
The situation is one of the wildest in gaming history, given the expected impact of GTA 6 in the market. The fact that one person, or group, potentially has a full build of the game ahead of launch and can post whatever they feel like, whenever they feel like it, is unprecedented, especially for a game of this scale. And there really is no other game of this scale. We’ll see what happens next, but for now, the GTA 6 official look on Netflix drops Thursday at 3 PM ET.
Update: Cyberleeks has just leaked a 4.5 minute clip of early Lucia footage that treads into story spoilers. It seems likely more is to come.
Here is the Rockstar statement in full:
![frase](https://images.forbes.com/fbs-games-assets/frase.png)
FEATURED | Frase ByForbes™
Unscramble The Anagram To Reveal The Phrase
![pinpoint](https://images.forbes.com/fbs-games-assets/pinpoint.png)
Pinpoint By Linkedin
Guess The Category
![queens](https://images.forbes.com/fbs-games-assets/queens.png)
Queens By Linkedin
Crown Each Region
![crossclimb](https://images.forbes.com/fbs-games-assets/crossclimb.png)
Crossclimb By Linkedin
Unlock A Trivia Ladder
“Dear all, We know that many of you have been waiting to hear from us regarding the events of the past week. It would be an understatement to say that having videos of Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay leak in this way has been heartbreaking for our team, and this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time. We are very sorry that everything has taken as long as it has — from getting the game finished (nearly there!) to sharing more details and official gameplay, and providing the community with everything you want to know.
We are very excited for everyone to see the extended look tomorrow. It has taken longer than we wanted to get it ready, but as with everything we do, we know we need to exceed your expectations, and we are determined to deliver at the level you expect and deserve. While it is unfortunate that the intended game experience may now be impacted by some spoilers, we hope that everyone will wait a bit longer to experience the game for themselves on November 19.
We want to thank everyone in the community who has reached out with messages of support this past week — your words have meant more to this team than you can imagine. Ultimately, we are making this game for you, and without you, we would not have the privilege of making games.
We look forward to sharing more with you soon. Sincerely, Rockstar Games”
Follow me on Twitter, YouTube, and Instagram.
Pick up my sci-fi novels the Herokiller series and The Earthborn Trilogy.
summary: Rockstar Games has issued its first public statement addressing persistent leaks of Grand Theft Auto 6 by a source known as Cyberleeks. Calling the situation heartbreaking, the company expressed disappointment that players are seeing the game this way months before launch. The statement preceded an official gameplay premiere and arrived as major story spoilers regarding the character Lucia began to surface.
key_points: Rockstar released a public statement addressing a week of ongoing GTA 6 leaks.
The leaks include early gameplay footage and growing story spoilers featuring the character Lucia.
Rockstar's statement did not address identifying or stopping the leaker.
The leak situation unfolded three months ahead of the game's scheduled release.

title: Xbox to let Insiders convert physical game discs into digital entitlements later this month
author: Vikki Blake
content:
Xbox will let Xbox Insiders begin testing a disc-to-digital feature from August 31, letting owners of supported physical games unlock a digital entitlement for the same title.
As announced on Xbox Wire, players can insert a supported disc into an Xbox One or Xbox Series X console and launch the game to claim the entitlement, with "Most Xbox One and Xbox Series X disc-based games" supported.
"This is part of our broader commitment to game preservation," said VP next generation, Jason Ronald.
"As technology, devices, and distribution continue to evolve, preserving access to the games people own matters more than ever."
Xbox Play Anywhere and Xbox Cloud Gaming become available on the unlocked copy where supported, and the physical disc isn't affected, it plays exactly as it did before. However, only one revokable digital license can be generated per game disc.
Xbox says it's starting with "thousands of titles" and will add more over time, though not every title will be available at launch.
The announcement lands a little under two months after Sharma told Xbox staff that the division's business is "not healthy." The company announced the divestment of five internal studios – Compulsion Games, Double Fine, Ninja Theory, Undead Labs, and Arkane – and cutting around 3,200 roles.
It also follows Sony's announcement last month that it planned to discontinue production of physical discs for new PlayStation games launching from January 2028. After that, games will be sold only in digital format, while titles released on disc before January 2028 will not be affected.
What isn't yet clear is how publishers and retailers factor into the scheme and whether third-party titles are included alongside first-party ones.
summary: Starting August 31, Xbox Insiders can test a new feature that allows owners of supported physical game discs to claim a digital entitlement for the same title. The initiative, aimed at game preservation, lets players insert a disc to unlock the digital version while leaving the physical disc fully functional. However, the physical disc can only be used to generate a single revokable digital license, and not all titles will be available at launch.
key_points: Xbox Insiders can begin testing the disc-to-digital conversion feature on August 31.
Players insert a supported disc into an Xbox One or Xbox Series X to claim the digital entitlement.
The physical disc remains playable as before, but only one digital license can be generated per disc.
The launch starts with thousands of titles, supporting features like Xbox Play Anywhere and Xbox Cloud Gaming where applicable.
