title: Galaxy S27 series design gets way more interesting in new leaked renders
author: Mihai Matei
content:
Last updated: August 24th, 2026 at 20:09 UTC+02:00
Still plenty of surprises left to uncover.
Asif Shaik - SamMobile
A few more design cues for the entire Galaxy S27 series have just been revealed through a series of fan-made CAD renders. According to leaks, next year's Galaxy S27 series might finally introduce a fourth main-series model and a new aesthetic for at least the Ultra.
In fact, apart from the redesigned camera housing, @UniverseIce says the Galaxy S27 Ultra will have almost the same overall dimensions as the S26 Ultra.
For reference, the latter measures 163.6 x 78.1 x 7.9mm and has a 6.9-inch display.
Ice Universe
Galaxy S27 Ultra CAD render
Moving on, beyond the redesigned camera housing, the Galaxy S27 Ultra will supposedly be relatively conservative in a couple of other key areas.
Namely, it apparently has the same S Pen holster and bottom speaker placement as the S26 Ultra — bottom-left.
Samsung has used this configuration for its Ultra models since the Galaxy Note 20 Ultra.
The rest of the upcoming S27 series does things a little differently, though. The source says the base S27, S27+, and S27 Pro have had the bottom speaker relocated from the left to the right side of the lower edge.
One render even shows an unusual S27 Pro design, and in a way, it's even more exciting than the Ultra. Let's check it out.
Disappointingly, some recent rumors suggest that the Galaxy S27 Pro will be more similar to the Plus than the Ultra. However, these new renders tell a different story, at least as far as the external design is concerned.
The one odd thing we noticed in these leaked renders is that the Galaxy S27 Pro also appears to have a brand-new camera housing design, similar to the S27 Ultra.
It looks wider but not quite as wide as the S27 Ultra's, nor as narrow as the usual vertical island beneath Samsung's camera rings.
Galaxy S27 Ultra CAD render, bottom
Galaxy S27 Pro CAD render, bottom
Galaxy S27 CAD render, bottom
Galaxy S27+ CAD render, bottom
This could be an error or a bad CAD, or more hopefully, it could be a hint that the Pro model, if it exists, may be a more compact replica of the Ultra. Samsung's Pro might be to the Ultra what the Apple iPhone 17 Pro is to the 17 Pro Max.
That may be too good to be true, though, and even if the S27 Pro has a new camera housing design, there's no guarantee the housing holds Ultra-grade camera hardware. For now, let's wait for more details before we draw any definitive conclusions based on this one CAD render.
Samsung should announce the Galaxy S27 series in early 2027, so there's plenty of time left to uncover its mysteries.
summary: Fan-made CAD renders have revealed new design cues for Samsung's upcoming Galaxy S27 series, including a potential fourth main-series model and a redesigned camera housing for the Ultra. The leaks indicate that while the S27 Ultra retains similar dimensions and layout to its predecessor, the base, S27+, and S27 Pro models feature relocated bottom speakers. Additionally, the Galaxy S27 Pro appears to feature a new camera housing design reminiscent of the Ultra, sparking speculation about its configuration.
key_points: The Galaxy S27 series may introduce a fourth main-series model and a new aesthetic for the Ultra.
The Galaxy S27 Ultra will feature nearly identical dimensions, S Pen holster, and bottom-left speaker placement as the S26 Ultra.
The base S27, S27+, and S27 Pro have their bottom speakers relocated from the left to the right side.
Leaked renders show the Galaxy S27 Pro with a brand-new camera housing design similar to the S27 Ultra.

title: The e-bike is the most complete expression of the bullying arrogance of cyclists
author: Stephen Bayley
content:
![Hundreds of Lime electric bicycles](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000494541930_17875910056820_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Hundreds of Lime electric bicycles](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000494541930_17875910056820_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
There are 75,000 e-bikes in London, and there are days when I get the impression that most of them have been brainlessly abandoned at the end of my road.
The concept of “dockless” e-bike carries – for some – a thrilling sense of care-free liberation, of being untethered from authority and practical constraints, of being unchained from the lunatic of regulations. A bicycling nirvana.
And that’s all true. But what it also means is that pedestrians have to pick their way through a tangle of wheels and handlebars, as if a Halford’s superstore has erupted on the street. Not every adopter of the exciting “dockless” concept, I have noticed, takes care to dock with social responsibility.
“Micro-mobility” means macro-inconvenience for the 10 million who are not of the 75,000. There are streets in central London where the pavement has wholly surrendered to the e-bike, as dangerous when stationary obstacles as they are when in motion and pedalled by a demented individual intent on maximising the value of the hire fee.
The wonder of it all is that no-one in authority seems to have anticipated the outcome. But we know in the matter of traffic management, TfL – and, indeed, provincial equivalents – conduct their business with a mixture of incompetence and malice.
A certain sign of systemic degeneration is chaotic transport. That’s where we are: the e-bike contributing generously to the anarchy of the roads.
Then there is the aesthetics, or what you might prefer to call terrible mess. Here the e-bike makes another significant contribution to the misery of the sensitive. There is nothing to be said, even ironically, for the benefits of clutter.
![Lime bikes lay in the road on March 27, 2024 in London, United Kingdom.](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/news/2026/08/24/TELEMMGLPICT000436252455_17875910469710_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqqVzuuqpFlyLIwiB6NTmJwfSVWeZ_vEN7c6bHu2jJnT8.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
People who care about urban housekeeping (and there are more than 75,000 of them) have for years been horrified by the visual pollution of overbearing, hectoring and redundant signage in our cities. Do this! Don’t do that! Smile, you’re on camera!
To the primeval forests of traffic-lights, poles and boards, sand-bags and cones can now be added the abandoned, static e-bikes making city life just that little bit more unpleasant for the majority.
But there is a general problem with bicycles of all kinds. God – or Nature – drives a hard bargain. In return for the beautiful and efficient theory of the bicycle which translates foot-power into smooth and silent propulsion, stabilised by benign gyroscopic forces, bicycles take up An Awful Lot of Space.
The problem of storage has not been solved, as hallways and verandas everywhere testify. Although a generation ago Brompton, manufacturers of the ingenious folding bike, offered an alternative to the clunky Borisbike: a system of elegantly designed deposit boxes to stow your compact machine neatly and politely.
This was too neat a solution for lazy authorities to consider. So Borisbikes were imported from Canada.
Untethered from authority means oblivious to traffic lights and innocent walkers. Total disdain for good manners. In this sense, the e-bike is the most complete expression of the cyclist’s arrogance.
In one generation, bicyclists have declined from being put-upon herbivores to becoming recklessly entitled, righteous, selfish bullies. E-bikes add dangerously high wattage to this forlorn caste.
summary: London's 75,000 dockless e-bikes have caused widespread street clutter, blocked pavements, and visual pollution for the city's pedestrians. The author argues that authorities failed to anticipate these problems, contributing to urban transport anarchy. Furthermore, irresponsible riders and the high volume of abandoned bikes reflect a growing sense of entitlement and arrogance among cyclists.
key_points: There are 75,000 e-bikes in London, often resulting in brainlessly abandoned vehicles on streets and pavements.
Dockless e-bikes create dangerous obstacles for pedestrians and cause severe visual clutter in urban areas.
Authorities, including Transport for London (TfL), are criticized for failing to manage or anticipate these transport issues.
Cyclists are characterized as having shifted from put-upon herbivores to recklessly entitled, selfish bullies amplified by e-bike wattage.

title: Warhammer 40k: A Legend Returns — New Space Marine Captain On Bike Revealed
author: Simon Berman
content:
Warhammer 40k: A Legend Returns — New Space Marine Captain On Bike Revealed
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wh40k-bike-header.jpg) 
A brand new kit is here for a venerable 40k hero. Get a closer look at the new Space Marine Captain!
It seems, unsurprisingly, that Codex: Space Marines may be near. We can tell from the roar of motors just over the horizon, heralding the return of a classic 40k character: the Space Marine Captain on Bike. Relegated to “Legends” status last edition, he’s back astride a new hog to join the recently revealed multi-part Outriders squad.
Revving Engines and Filling Gaps
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wh40k-marine-captain-bike.jpg)
He’s back, and he’s, err, he’s just fine. I’m not gonna lie, this is not the most exciting of models. If I was choosing a model to (presumably) kick off the lead-up to the release of the 11th edition Codex: Space Marines, I probably would have picked a model with a little more mustard on it. With that said, it’s a nice enough model and does fill one of very few gaps in the Space Marine model range.
Outriders have been a big part of the marine aesthetic since the early days of 40k. There’s just something charmingly ridiculous about a guy in power armor racing across the battlefield to decapitate an ork with a chainsword. It’s a nod to medieval knights on horseback and is an appealing part of all Marine chapters to one degree or another.
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wh40k-marine-bikes-photo.jpg)
Some chapters get more out of this kind of model than others. White Scars, Blood Angels, Dark Angels, and to some degree, Raven Guard all get good use out of the fast assault capabilities of an outrider squad. So, being able to attach a Captain to one unit and a Chaplain to another does offer some pretty mean, fast-moving melee support for any army. He does offer a bonus of Cleave 1 to his attached unit, which does add up to a pretty solid amount of attacks against horde armies like Tyranids or Orks.
At the end of the day, this is a “meat and potatoes” character option that’s nice to have back in the range, even if it’s not the most exciting model reveal of the year.
Astartes Chopper
Now, where this kit does get interesting is in its options. Like the upcoming Outriders kit, the bike itself has some limited posability. It can be built racing forwards or at rest with the bike tilted as the captain braces his foot and lines up a shot or gestures with his melee weapon.
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wh40k-marine-captain-bike-alts.jpg)
More excitingly, the kit includes a variety of weapon options. The Captain’s right hand can wield your choice of power sword, thunder hammer (it’s gonna be this one, isn’t it?), or plasma pistol. As a nice little bonus, if you choose the plasma pistol, the kit includes a sheathed sword for full WYSIWYG goodness.
The kit also includes a choice of five heads. Two helmeted and two bare; no matter the aesthetics of your chapter of choice, there’s a strong option here. I’m particularly fond of the one with a bionic eye, myself/
All in all, a necessary if not particularly sexy addition to Space Marine armies. It’s nice to see a model return from the oubliette of Legends status, though. I recently painted up a unit of outriders for my Blood Angels and found them fun models to paint, so there’s a non-zero chance I pick up another when the new kit arrives. With two squads of outriders, I suppose I might add a Captain and Chaplain to each. I’m kind of a sucker for extremely specialized detachments, so maybe something cool awaits in the codex?
Will we see bike-mounted librarians and apothecaries next?
![Simon Berman](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/avatar-simon-berman-300x300-1-150x150.jpg)
summary: Games Workshop has revealed a new Space Marine Captain on Bike kit for Warhammer 40k, signaling that a new Codex: Space Marines may be approaching. Although considered a conventional model that is not overly flashy, it successfully fills a previous gap in the miniature range. The new kit features multiple build options, including posable bike configurations, various weapon choices like a thunder hammer or power sword, and a selection of five heads.
key_points: A classic Space Marine Captain on Bike has returned from Legends status with a new kit.
The model provides fast-moving melee support and grants a Cleave 1 bonus to its attached unit.
The kit offers limited bike posability, allowing it to be built racing forward or at rest.
Players can choose from several weapon options including a power sword, thunder hammer, or plasma pistol.
The box includes a choice of five heads, consisting of helmeted and bare variants.

title: Protesting PS5 Players Now Plan Permanent Blackout, Meaning No GTA 6 or Wolverine
author: Push Square; Sammy Barker
content:
![Furious PS5 Players Unplug Their Consoles in Protest Against Sony 1](https://images.pushsquare.com/69d52814c6f59/furious-ps5-players-unplug-their-consoles-in-protest-against-sony-1.900x.jpg)
Update []:
Angry PS5 players now propose an “indefinite” boycott of Sony’s console, as the previously planned blackout steps up its intensity.
In updated language, protesters say the originally mentioned window of 23rd August through 30th August is now “a minimum requirement”.
“Everyone is encouraged to go indefinitely until Sony change course,” the Does It Play account, a leader in the protest, writes. “Pedal to the metal or we won't get anywhere!”
Major upcoming PS5 games include The Blood of Dawnwalker, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Marvel’s Wolverine, Control Resonant, and GTA 6 – among many others.
It’s going to be really interesting to see how resolute campaigners remain in the face of an increasingly strong release schedule.
Original Story: Irate PS5 players have started unplugging their consoles all around the world, as a protest against Sony gets underway.
The blackout – technically scheduled to start at 7pm local time, but already being observed by many participants – is designed to reduce the Japanese giant’s active users, a key performance metric for the company.
Campaigners suggest participants should keep their consoles unplugged from today through 30th August as a minimum. That means no logins, no gaming, and certainly no spending through the PS Store.
While the protest is primarily aimed at Sony’s decision to cease manufacturing physical discs in January 2028, organisers also argue that the company has grown “further apart from its fan base”.
Earlier this week, a Push Square poll concluded 92% of enthusiasts believe PS Studios would benefit from new management, after stories emerged it was rebooting development on spin-off game Horizon Hunters Gathering.
As of its most recent financial report, Sony attracted around 125 million monthly active users, an increase year-over-year. I think this number would have to drop precipitously to have any kind of effect.
Speaking with investors about potential boycotts and PS Plus cancellations, Sony’s CFO Lin Tao said it’s not seeing any “impact on our business”.
This organised and widely publicised blackout campaign may be protesters’ best opportunity to get the company’s attention, then. Will you be taking part?
summary: Furious PS5 players are participating in a blackout protest against Sony by unplugging their consoles and avoiding the platform. Originally scheduled for a single week, organizers are now calling for an indefinite boycott until Sony changes course. The protest is primarily driven by Sony's decision to cease physical disc manufacturing in January 2028, alongside broader concerns about the company's disconnect from its fanbase.
key_points: PS5 players are protesting against Sony by keeping their consoles unplugged.
The protest aims to reduce Sony's monthly active user numbers and prevent spending on the PS Store.
Organizers have escalated the action from a one-week blackout to an indefinite boycott.
The core grievance involves Sony's plan to stop manufacturing physical discs in January 2028.
Sony's CFO previously stated that the business has seen no impact from potential boycotts.

title: iPhone 18 series prices confirmed to go up due to rising memory chip cost
author: Ro
content:
After introducing a notable price hike to its Mac and iPad lineup back in June due to an unbearable memory chip price increase, the word on the street is that this year's iPhones will follow suit. In fact, a report from earlier this month says all iPhones from the 18 series will cost $100 more than their predecessors.
The most recent report on the matter, however, comes from a more reputable source, and it confirms the earlier claims from other tipsters. The increasing RAM and NAND chip prices are pressuring Apple to act and pass some of the cost onto consumers.
People familiar with the matter claim that Apple was trying to avoid a price hike and absorb the cost, but it can no longer sustain its slim profit margins, so a $100 increase on all iPhone 18 prices means the company can share the cost with its consumers without outpricing the competition like Samsung. After all, Samsung, Google and other smartphone manufacturers have already hiked their prices, so Apple doing so won't be frowned upon.
Even though the iPhone 18 Pro could start at $1,199, it will stay well within the competitors' price bracket. Additionally, the loyal Apple user base will likely allow Apple to increase prices further down the road if needed, so even if it sounds like a lot at first, a $100 price increase for the new iPhones is actually a conservative adjustment in today's context.
Now even lesser people will be interested in buying
summary: Apple is reportedly planning to increase the prices of all iPhone 18 models by $100 due to rising memory chip costs. The company had initially tried to absorb the expenses, but unsustainable profit margins and industry-wide price hikes by competitors like Samsung and Google have forced the adjustment. This change will bring the starting price of the iPhone 18 Pro to an estimated $1,199 while keeping it competitive.
key_points: All iPhone 18 series models are expected to cost $100 more than their predecessors.
Rising RAM and NAND chip costs have pressured Apple to pass expenses onto consumers.
Apple previously increased prices for its Mac and iPad lineups in June due to memory chip costs.
Competitors such as Samsung and Google have already raised their smartphone prices.
The iPhone 18 Pro is anticipated to start at $1,199 while remaining competitive.

title: Apple's Foldable iPhone Reportedly Impressed Early Testers
author: Jibin Joseph
content:
![](https://sm.pcmag.com/t/pcmag_uk/news/a/apples-fol/apples-foldable-iphone-reportedly-impressed-early-testers_3kcv.1920.jpg) (Credit: Jeffrey Hazelwood/PCMag)
We’re weeks away from the potential launch of Apple’s first foldable, and a new report based on early impressions suggests the device is one of Apple’s most exciting products in recent years.
The rumored iPhone Ultra is expected to feature a passport-style form factor similar to Samsung’s recently launched Galaxy Z Fold 8, along with a nearly crease-free 7.8-inch internal display, a 5.5-inch cover display, and a dual-camera system on the rear.
People who have already tried the device are impressed with how it fits in their pockets, the durability of the hinge, and the iPad-like layout of the internal display, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. Some testers also noted that the Ultra excels as a camera viewfinder, while performing decently across gaming, productivity, and entertainment.
Gurman expects the iPhone Ultra to popularize the foldables segment and convince some users to purchase one. They may, however, face two major drawbacks. First, since the Ultra only offers a dual-camera setup, some users may miss the telephoto lens for optical zoom. Second, those accustomed to Face ID may not enjoy going back to the Touch ID fingerprint sensor, he says.
As always, there’s a lot of buzz around Apple’s entry into a new segment. The company is expected to unveil the foldable at its annual fall event, rumored for Sept. 8, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro models. According to multiple leakers, the iPhone Ultra will be available in limited supply at launch and could be priced above $2,000.
Gurman also noted that Apple may increase the price of other iPhones due to rising memory costs. It raised prices of its Macs, iPads, and Vision Pro for the same reason in June.
summary: Apple's rumored first foldable iPhone, expected to be called the iPhone Ultra, has reportedly impressed early testers with its passport-style design, hinge durability, and internal display. According to a report by Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, the device is slated for a potential launch at Apple's September 8 event, though it may face drawbacks like lacking a telephoto lens and using Touch ID instead of Face ID. The foldable could be priced above $2,000 with limited supply at launch, and rising memory costs may also lead to price increases for other Apple iPhones.
key_points: The rumored iPhone Ultra features a passport-style form factor with a 7.8-inch internal display and a 5.5-inch cover display.
Early testers praised the device's pocket-friendly size, hinge durability, and iPad-like internal layout.
Potential drawbacks include a dual-camera system lacking a telephoto lens and a return to Touch ID instead of Face ID.
The foldable is rumored to launch around September 8, with a price tag above $2,000 and limited availability.
Rising memory costs could drive up the price of other upcoming iPhone models as well.

title: Microsoft Announces New 'Xbox Gear' Merchandise Including Tees, Hoodies & Hats
author: Pure Xbox; Fraser Gilbert
content:
![The Xbox Gear Shop Is Back, And It's Full Of New Tees, Hoodies & Hats](https://images.purexbox.com/130fe87b5c0cc/the-xbox-gear-shop-is-back-and-its-full-of-new-tees-hoodies-and-hats.900x.jpg)
Anyone up for some new Xbox merch?
Microsoft has announced a new range of t-shirts, sweaters, hoodies and hats today that are "inspired by the history, creativity, and community that have helped shape XBOX over the past 25 years", from 2001 all the way up to 2026.
The new range is split into three categories — Gloss, Est.01, and Blood Gulch — and they range from basic designs with the new Xbox logo or literally the words "Est.01" on the front, to quite elaborate offerings that highlight the history of the brand. The Blood Gulch Hoodie is probably our favourite of the bunch here at $74.99.
Here's just a small sample of the kind of "Xbox Gear" on offer so far:
![The Xbox Gear Shop Is Back, And It's Full Of New Tees, Hoodies & Hats 2](https://images.purexbox.com/a69c47b2de567/the-xbox-gear-shop-is-back-and-its-full-of-new-tees-hoodies-and-hats-2.900x.jpg)
If you're interested, you can head over to the Xbox Gear website right now to see what's available, and Microsoft says that "additional drops" are already planned that will "continue to offer new ways for fans to celebrate the moments, memories, and community that have shaped XBOX over the past 25 years".
Don't forget that the Xbox Game Studios Shop has its own kind of merchandise for specific Xbox first-party games as well, so you can get clothing for the likes of Gears, Halo and Forza over there.
We'll leave you with a bit more of today's statement, and tell us in the comments if you're planning to buy anything!
"To help mark 25 years of XBOX, we’re excited to introduce XBOX Gear, the new home for official XBOX-branded merchandise. Available now at gear.xbox.com, XBOX Gear features original collections inspired by the history, creativity, and community that have helped shape XBOX over the past 25 years. At launch, fans can explore three new collections: Gloss, Est.01, and Blood Gulch, ranging from brand essentials and XBOX history to design-forward apparel that explores new creative territory."
summary: Microsoft has launched a new official Xbox Gear merchandise collection featuring t-shirts, sweaters, hoodies, and hats to mark 25 years of the brand. The new lineup is split into three categories: Gloss, Est.01, and Blood Gulch. Additional product drops are already planned for the future, and fans can currently purchase items on the Xbox Gear website.
key_points: Microsoft announced a new range of official Xbox-branded merchandise including t-shirts, sweaters, hoodies, and hats.
The initial launch is split into three distinct categories: Gloss, Est.01, and Blood Gulch.
The apparel is inspired by the history, creativity, and community of Xbox over the past 25 years.
Additional merchandise drops are already planned for the future.
Fans can purchase the current items directly from the Xbox Gear website.

title: 'This Is Illegal': Stop Killing Games Movement Distances Itself from GTA 6 Leaks
author: Push Square; Stephen Tailby
content:
!['This Is Illegal': Stop Killing Games Movement Distances Itself from GTA 6 Leaks 1](https://images.pushsquare.com/6950209db6f11/this-is-illegal-stop-killing-games-movement-distances-itself-from-gta-6-leaks-1.900x.jpg)
This week will see the debut of an extended look at GTA 6, our first official glimpse of the game itself ahead of launch later in the year.
Unfortunately, a spate of leaked videos of the game have emerged online over the last week or so, thanks to a person (or group) calling themselves Cyberleek.
Cyberleek states that its goals are to push back against things like digital pre-orders, single player content being gated off, and games not being playable once online servers go down.
These are similar issues that the legal movement Stop Killing Games opposes, but the group has distanced itself from Cyberleek and their actions with a lengthy statement on social media.
In a nutshell, Stop Killing Games doesn't condone the leaks at all, and urges people not to engage; while Cyberleek's purported manifesto sounds noble, it's actually pushing a crypto currency and asking people to pay up for more leaks.
"The group is using the leak to promote a memecoin, attaching crypto links and QR codes to the footage and asking people to pay for more," the statement reads. "Do not send these people your money, no matter how much sympathy you may feel for their actions. This is illegal, and frankly, we feel for everyone at Rockstar having to go through this ordeal again, especially just over a week before Rockstar’s own official 'Extended Look' premieres."
"Using illegal means to make a point is unacceptable to us and does nothing to protect our right to keep using what we paid for. No matter how strongly you disagree with the decisions of upper management at these companies, there are still thousands of developers who worked hard on this project — and they’re the ones being hit the hardest."
Stop Killing Games also points out that leaks against Rockstar Games rarely work out, pointing to 2022's GTA 6 leak that resulted in one of the culprits being sentenced to an indefinite hospital order.
"This isn't a cause worth risking your money or your future on," Stop Killing Games says.
Again, the official extended look arrives in a few days, and there seems to be no plan from Take-Two and Rockstar to change course.
summary: The Stop Killing Games movement has publicly distanced itself from a group called Cyberleek, which recently leaked footage of GTA 6 online. Although Cyberleek claimed to fight against issues like server shutdowns and gated single-player content, Stop Killing Games condemned the leaks as illegal and exploitative. The group noted that Cyberleek is using the leaked footage to promote a cryptocurrency and demand payment for more content.
key_points: Cyberleek leaked GTA 6 videos online ahead of Rockstar's official extended look.
Stop Killing Games issued a statement condemning the leaks and urging people not to engage or send money.
Cyberleek is reportedly using the leaks to promote a cryptocurrency and charge for additional footage.
Stop Killing Games emphasized that illegal actions harm hardworking developers rather than upper management.

title: If these Galaxy S27 Ultra renders are accurate, Samsung can't stop Apple copycat claims
author: Hadlee Simons
content:
If these Galaxy S27 Ultra renders are accurate, Samsung can't stop Apple copycat claims
Aug 24, 2026 — 2:14 AM ET
![Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra and Apple iPhone 16 Pro Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra and Apple iPhone 16 Pro](https://www.androidauthority.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Samsung-Galaxy-S26-Ultra-and-Apple-iPhone-16-Pro.jpg)
- A tipster has posted apparent Galaxy S27 Ultra renders online.
- The pictures show a Galaxy phone with an iPhone-like camera plateau.
- The images also seem to hint at integrated magnets for Qi2 charging and other accessories.
Samsung is expected to launch the Galaxy S27 series early next year, and we’ve already heard a few rumors about the new phones. However, the latest leak may have given us a good look at the Galaxy S27 Ultra itself.
Tipster Sonny Dickson posted apparent Galaxy S27 Ultra renders on X, showing a major departure from the Galaxy S26 Ultra design. Check out the images below.
The images show a phone with a camera bump similar to the iPhone 17 Pro camera housings. That means we’ve got a camera plateau here, stretching across the back of the phone. Apple wasn’t the first brand to adopt such a design (Xiaomi and others offered wide camera plateaus years ago), but it can’t be a coincidence that Samsung might be taking this route.
What do you think of the S27 Ultra's apparent design?
Otherwise, the pictures show a pill-shaped cutout on the plateau, which is ostensibly for a secondary camera and flash. We also see a circular cutout on the rear cover, suggesting that the phone will have integrated magnets for Qi2 wireless charging and accessories.
Dickson also claims that the Galaxy S27 Ultra will be available in “two different sizes.” We previously heard that the Galaxy S27 Pro was on the cards and could be a compact flagship with some Ultra features. So we’re guessing the tipster is referring to this rumored Pro model.
summary: Apparent renders of the Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra shared by tipster Sonny Dickson suggest a major redesign that resembles Apple's camera plateau style. The leaked images also indicate the presence of integrated magnets for Qi2 charging and accessories, alongside claims that the phone will come in two sizes. Samsung is expected to launch the Galaxy S27 series early next year.
key_points: Tipster Sonny Dickson posted leaked renders of the Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra.
The renders show an iPhone-like camera plateau stretching across the back of the phone.
The images suggest the device will feature integrated magnets for Qi2 wireless charging and accessories.
The leaks also claim the Galaxy S27 Ultra will be available in two different sizes.

title: Warhammer 40k: Space Marines Codex Moves 16 Units To Legendary Status!
author: Simon Berman
content:
Warhammer 40k: Space Marines Codex Moves 16 Units To Legendary Status!
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/40k-marine-classic-skull-header.jpg) 
Some universe-shaking changes are coming for Space Marines this fall.
Just an hour after the reveal of the new Outrider Captain, a full preview of the new Codex: Space Marines is here! The studio kicked things off with a brief video overview of what to expect, so take a few minutes to watch and let’s dig into it. There’s a lot to consider!
A New Vision of Space Marine Armies
First and foremost, the overall Space Marine army is being subtly reenvisioned. It seems that a primary goal of the 40k devs this edition is to return Space Marines to the feeling of a powerful elite force, but few in number. Points increases are coming for many units, though the specifics of those changes are yet to be revealed.
However, we do know that as part of this overall shift, Space Marine unit profiles are changing. In order to better simulate the superhuman prowess of the Astartes, their core stat lines are getting some significant buffs.
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/wh40k-intercessors.jpg)
Beginning with the basic Intercessor, we can see some big changes. These core troops have had their Toughness increased to a solid 5, putting them on par with Orks and letting them slug it out with heavy-hitting enemies. Simultaneously, they’re also seeing the strength of their melee attacks increasing. Chainswords and the basic knives and fists profile both increase to Strength 5, which also puts them on even footing with Orks. However, their basic weapon, the Bolt Rifle, now has two firing modes, one that is also Strength 5 but with a secondary “Focused Fire” profile bringing them to Strength 6!
We haven’t seen a full statline increase for Phobos armored troops, but we’ve learned a little. Their Toughness remains 4 given their lighter armor, but they compensate by gaining a significant movement boost to 8″, allowing them to rapidly capture objectives or carry out crucial actions. We’ve also received a teaser for the new Terminator profile, which includes Toughness 6 (!) and Strength 5 storm bolters. In tandem with the Tacticus armored Intercessors, Space Marine players will have strong options to build whatever kind of force they desire.
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/99070101045_SMPrimarisLieutenantinPhobosArmour03.jpg) 
We also learned of a few new kits, including a new multi-part Intercessor kit (with back banner!), as well as the individual release of the Marines first released in the Armageddon box set. Details are thin on the ground beyond that, so we’ll just have to see what else is coming.
Heretics and Codex-Divergent Changes
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Huron-Blackheart-and-the-Masters-of-the-Maelstrom-image-2026-e1775761790559.jpg)
Fortunately for those of us who don’t play Codex-compliant marines, they’re all getting stat bonuses at the same time. A huge update is coming for Heretic Astartes, and non-Codex-compliant chapters like Blood Angels and Space Wolves, along with the main Codex update. All of these units will receive similar stat and weapon changes to bring them in line with the new baseline for Space Marines. Presumably, their points will also increase, but those details remain to be seen.
The 40k app is really coming into its own with this sort of update, which will prevent Chaos Marines from feeling underpowered until they receive their own codex later in the lifetime of the edition.
A Farewell to Arms
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2016/09/99120101128_spacemarinetacticalsquadreformat01.jpg)
Unsurprisingly, a number of the oldest marine units are moving from the core line to “Legendary” status. However, a number of these models will inhabit an entirely new status as “Legendary Proxies”.
- Tactical Squad – counts as an Intercessor Squad
- Devastator Squad – counts as a Desolation Squad
- Suppressor Squad – counts as an Inceptor Squad
- Pedro Kantor – counts as a Captain
- Uriel Ventris – counts as a Captain
Interesting stuff here and I wonder if it’s not a stopgap before we see some of these return as full Primarisified kits over the course of the edition. Given the prominence of the Crimson Fists in the Armageddon campaign book it’s hard to imagine we’ve seen the last of Pedro Kantor!
![](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2018/11/99800101063_PedroKantorNEW01.jpg) 
Beyond that list, a number of units are moving to the standard “Legends” format. Their rules are still part of the game and can be found in the official app for army building but their models will no longer be for sale.
- Centurion Assault Squad
- Centurion Devastator Squad
- Razorback
- Predator Destructor
- Predator Annihilator
- Vindicator
- Whirlwind
- Stormhawk Interceptor
- Stormtalon Gunship
- Stormraven Gunship
- Hammerfall Bunker
I’m sad to see smaller tanks leaving the main line (for now, at least) but I admit I’m maliciously pleased to see the last of my least favorite models in all of 40k, the Centurions, go the way of the dodo. Let us never speak of them again.
New land raider kit, please.
![Simon Berman](https://www.belloflostsouls.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/avatar-simon-berman-300x300-1-150x150.jpg)
summary: The new Codex: Space Marines re-envisions the army as a powerful, elite, but fewer-in-number force, bringing stat buffs and points increases to units. Core stat lines are increasing across Space Marines, Heretic Astartes, and non-Codex-compliant chapters to better simulate superhuman prowess. Additionally, 16 older marine units are being moved to Legendary status, with some functioning as proxies while others transition out of regular sales.
key_points: Space Marine unit profiles are receiving significant stat buffs, including increased Toughness and melee strength for core troops like Intercessors.
Heretic Astartes and non-Codex-compliant chapters like Blood Angels and Space Wolves will receive similar stat and weapon updates alongside the main Codex.
A total of 16 older Space Marine units are moving to Legendary status, with specific models acting as proxies for newer squads.
Models moving to the standard Legends format, such as various tanks and the Centurion squads, will no longer be for sale though their rules remain in the official app.

title: Apple iPhone Ultra foldable reportedly wins over early testers
author: Sambit Saha
content:
According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, people who have been able to use the iPhone Fold, or Ultra, have been left thoroughly impressed by the device. Who exactly these people are, and whether or not their testimonies are honest, is up for debate.
Gurman has a pretty reliable track record with Apple's internal affairs and product development cycles, which does lend some meaningful credibility to the story. Through his latest PowerOn newsletter, the analyst has revealed the aforementioned people were quite happy with how the iPhone Ultra feels in the hand, and how fits in the pocket.
The early testers were also impressed with the device's hinge, and the overall durability of the whole setup. The system's UI was also praised, which will be taking advantage of the large inner display to feature iPadOS-style multitasking capabilities.
![Leaked dummy units of the iPhone Ultra fodlable have long confimred its form factor and size.](https://www.notebookcheck.net/fileadmin/_processed_/4/d/csm_apple_iphone_ultra_foldable_dummy_f7146a8945.jpg)
Mark also notes that the Samsung Z Fold 8 (currently $1,899.99 on Amazon) features a very similar form factor, so Apple's "wide" approach for its first foldable is not all that unique or novel anymore. The Z Fold 8 has definitely received overwhelmingly warm responses from the community, which certainly inspires confidence in the form factor.
However, like the Z Fold 8, the iPhone Ultra foldable will only feature a dual-camera setup, forgoing its telephoto lens. While some people may be okay with it, others will find it hard to digest that a $2,000+ smartphone misses out on a feature which the iPhone family has had for almost a decade now.
Other notable details of the upcoming iPhone Ultra foldable, according to industry sources, include a 5.5-inch outer display, a 7.8-ish inch inner display, roughly 9.4-mm thickness (folded), A20 Pro SoC and dual 48 MP shooters.
![The iPhone Ultra foldable is likely to be around 9.4 mm thin when folded.](https://www.notebookcheck.net/fileadmin/_processed_/1/b/csm_apple_iphone_ultra_foldable_render__c6f9379702.jpg)
summary: According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, early testers of Apple's upcoming iPhone Ultra foldable have been thoroughly impressed by the device. The testers praised its hand-feel, pocketability, hinge, durability, and iPadOS-style multitasking UI. However, the device is expected to feature a dual-camera setup without a telephoto lens, despite its anticipated price of over $2,000.
key_points: Early testers were impressed with the iPhone Ultra foldable's design, hinge, durability, and UI.
The device features a wide form factor similar to the Samsung Z Fold 8.
The foldable is expected to include a dual-camera setup instead of a telephoto lens.
Reported specifications include a 5.5-inch outer display, a 7.8-inch inner display, and an A20 Pro SoC.

title: The Witcher 4 Release Date Confirmed, Gamescom Songs of the Past Showcase Announced
author: Digital Foundry; William Judd
content:
![Ciri in The Witcher 4](https://images.digitalfoundry.net/d40071fa165d7/ciri-in-the-witcher-4.970x.jpg)
Four years after first revealing the game, CD Projekt Red has finally announced a release date for The Witcher 4: 2028. The news comes from joint CEO Michał Nowakowski via Twitter, alongside an invitation to a Witcher 3: Songs of the Past showcase taking place tomorrow - as part of Opening Night Live at Gamescom in Cologne, Germany.
The CDPR announcement is two minutes in length, with Nowakowski promising a prominent presence in hall eight at the trade show, which opens for journalists and trade visitors from Wednesday and is open to the public from Thursday onwards.
The physical presence at Gamescom and the livestream appearance will be focused around the upcoming Songs of the Past expansion for The Witcher 3, including details on its story and "content". The expansion was previously announced to arrive sometime in 2027.
The Witcher 4 update is that the Ciri-centred game currently has a developer count of over 500, with a "huge and immersive open world, intense and action-packed gameplay, and a deep impactful story", according to Nowakowski. It sounds like there won't be any further information on the game at the show, but you never know.
Are you planning to play Songs of the Past, or are you waiting for The Witcher 4? Let me know in the comments below, and stay tuned for more Gamescom announcements as we have them!
summary: CD Projekt Red joint CEO Michał Nowakowski announced that The Witcher 4 will be released in 2028, four years after the game's initial reveal. The Ciri-centered title currently has over 500 developers working on its open world and gameplay. Additionally, CDPR announced a Gamescom showcase for The Witcher 3's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion, which launches in 2027.
key_points: CD Projekt Red announced a 2028 release date for The Witcher 4.
The Witcher 4 features a Ciri-centered story and currently has a development team of over 500 people.
A showcase for The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion is scheduled for Gamescom's Opening Night Live.
The Songs of the Past expansion was previously announced for a 2027 release.

title: Major Garmin Launch Coming Tomorrow: Garmin Fenix 9 Expected
author: Andrew Williams
content:
Garmin is set to announce something big tomorrow, and you can watch the unveil live. It’s set to stream on YouTube in a new kind of reveal for the brand, and many think this marks the arrival of the Garmin Fenix 9.
The YouTube Premiere stream will begin at 7am ET, for what Garmin is calling a “groundbreaking launch event.”
But what is it for? Garmin has left just a few clues in the teasers for this launch.
First up, there’s the tagline “your playground is calling. Now’s the time to answer.” It’s a pretty vague tease, but the accompanying image suggests it’s part of the wider running category.
We see a young man with a hydration vest running through a scenic chunk of the great outdoors, although the image is a little too low-res to make out what he is wearing on his wrist. The first assumption is, after all, that this “groundbreaking” launch is going to be an update to one the company’s higher profile watch series.
The other, not-all-that-useful, hint is seen in the YouTube page’s description, which bears the “BeatYesterday” hashtag.
“Dedicated to helping people make the most of the time they spend pursuing their passions, we believe every day is an opportunity to innovate and a chance to #BeatYesterday," it reads
Garmin has in the past used this hashtag as part of its advertising campaigns to support its adventuring watches.
Lines in this wider family include Instinct, Enduro, Tactix, Marq and Fenix. This may be hopeful thinking, but taking a bold new approach to the launch may suggest we’re looking at the most anticipated update of the lot here, the Garmin Fenix 9.
Garmin Fenix 9: What Is Known So Far
An FCC filing for what is believed to be the Fenix 9 was spotted earlier this month, suggesting the watch is indeed heading for a release soon.
That documentation suggests mobile internet and satellite communication will both be options. A Czech retailer also briefly listed options for the watch, suggesting it will come in 43mm, 47mm and 51mm sizes.
This is a pretty standard spread, as seen in the Fenix 8 family too.
There’s still a big question mark over what’s new in the Garmin Fenix 9, then, but there may not be long to wait until all is revealed:
Garmin’s YouTube Premiere page for the announcement is already live — give it a bookmark if you want to witness the reveal as it happens. Garmin Fenix 9, or something else entirely? Place your bets.
summary: Garmin is hosting a live YouTube Premiere event tomorrow at 7am ET for what it describes as a groundbreaking launch. Teasers suggest the announcement relates to an adventuring or running watch, with widespread expectations pointing toward the arrival of the Garmin Fenix 9. Recent leaks, including an FCC filing and a brief retailer listing, indicate the new watch may feature mobile internet, satellite communication, and come in 43mm, 47mm, and 51mm sizes.
key_points: Garmin is streaming a groundbreaking launch event on YouTube tomorrow at 7am ET.
Teaser materials suggest the product belongs to the brand's running and adventuring watch category.
An FCC filing suggests the upcoming device will include mobile internet and satellite communication options.
A brief Czech retailer listing indicated the watch will be offered in 43mm, 47mm, and 51mm sizes.

title: Gurman: Early iPhone Ultra testers praise its design, hinge and usability
author: Siddharth
content:

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, citing people who have internally tested the upcoming foldable iPhone, has outlined several aspects of the device that impressed early testers.

title: The Galaxy S27 Ultra looks like an outright iPhone copy in this latest leak
author: Sanuj Bhatia
content:
![Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra sky blue cameras](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/HFLKfPMSoWGqmUUaAm5rHo.jpg) 
What you need to know
- Early Galaxy S27 Ultra leaks point to a major redesign with a horizontal camera plateau similar to the iPhone 17 Pro.
- Samsung could finally bring native Qi2 support to the Galaxy S27 Ultra, with magnets seemingly visible in leaked renders.
- The Galaxy S27 Ultra could reportedly launch in two sizes, potentially giving buyers a smaller Ultra option for the first time.
With the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series out of the way, attention is now turning toward Samsung's next flagship smartphone lineup. And if the latest round of leaks is anything to go by, the Galaxy S27 Ultra could be getting a major redesign that looks a lot like Apple's latest iPhones.
For the past few years, Samsung has stuck with a vertical camera layout across its Galaxy S lineup. In fact, the company has been criticized several times for shipping very similar-looking Galaxy S Ultra phones year after year. It now looks like Samsung is finally planning to move away from that design, but perhaps not in the direction everyone expected.
Leakers Sonny Dickson, Max Jambor, and Ice Universe have shared what is claimed to be the Galaxy S27 Ultra's new design on X, and it's hard not to see the resemblance to Apple's iPhone 17 Pro lineup.
The leaked design shows a horizontal camera plateau across the back, similar to the latest iPhones, with two large camera rings and an elongated section that will likely house the remaining cameras and LED flash.
 ![Leaked renders of the Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/TvEEMqRZbxE63kbediJYY4.jpg) 
It's pretty clear where Samsung may be taking some design inspiration from this time around. On the bright side, though, the leaked renders also appear to show a Qi2 magnetic ring on the back, suggesting Samsung could finally build native Qi2 support directly into the Galaxy S27 Ultra.
The leaks also suggest Samsung could offer the Galaxy S27 Ultra in two different sizes, something we've heard rumored previously. If true, that could mean we're finally getting a more compact version of Samsung's Ultra flagship alongside the larger model.
Of course, we're still months away from the Galaxy S27 series launch, and plenty could change before Samsung makes anything official. But these early leaks certainly suggest Samsung is preparing a pretty major design shake-up, even if the inspiration appears to be coming straight from Cupertino.

title: Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra will come in two sizes, according to CAD models
author: Alexander Fagot
content:
Samsung will apparently surprise us with a new camera design for its Galaxy S27 series next year, though it may face significant criticism for a design choice, that clearly resembles other smartphone designs, primarily of course, Apple’s iPhone 17 Pro. And that may not be the only similarity between Samsung's next Ultra flagship and the two differently sized iPhone Pro models.
As the well-known leaker Sonny Dickson points out based on two slightly different CAD models, Samsung appears to be planning two different sizes for the Galaxy S27 Ultra as well, though it’s currently unclear whether the smaller model is the rumored Galaxy S27 Pro or if there will actually be two Ultra models with different sizes, as suggested by Sonny and Ice’s X posts based on the relative positions of the buttons on the side.
Camera redesign brings new camera hardware
Setting aside the design aspect, a refresh of Samsung's camera hardware, which has remained virtually unchanged for many years is obviously a positive development. In particular, the 3x telephoto based on a small 1/3.94-inch 10-megapixel sensor seems outdated and is likely being dropped in 2027, which will free up space for larger batteries and potentially magnets around the Qi2 charging coil. According to past leaks, the four-year-old ISOCELL HP2 behind the camera is likely to be replaced with a more modern 200-megapixel sensor such as the ISOCELL HPC, which will also be responsible for the 3x–5x zoom performance in the future.
Update 24.08.2026 14:00 Smaller model is the Galaxy S27 Pro
Ice Universe has now "confirmed" that the smaller version of the Galaxy S27 Ultra is actually the Galaxy S27 Pro, which means there won't be two Ultra-models after all. Instead both the S27 Ultra and the S27 Pro get the new camera plateau design, according to his information. This is still not an official confirmation though, so take that with a grain of salt.
summary: According to CAD models and leaks, Samsung's Galaxy S27 series will feature a new camera design resembling the iPhone 17 Pro. Leaks indicate that the lineup will include a smaller Galaxy S27 Pro alongside the S27 Ultra rather than two different Ultra sizes. The update is also expected to bring refreshed camera hardware, dropping the old 3x telephoto sensor for a more modern 200-megapixel sensor.
key_points: Samsung's Galaxy S27 series will feature a new camera design similar to the iPhone 17 Pro.
Leaks based on CAD models initially suggested two Ultra sizes, but the smaller model is actually the Galaxy S27 Pro.
The outdated 3x telephoto sensor is expected to be dropped in favor of a modern 200-megapixel sensor.
The hardware changes may free up space for larger batteries and magnets around the Qi2 charging coil.
